## 53. The cut: a scene is covered before it is one form (ruled 2026-09-19)

Ruled 2026-09-19. Carried from Part XI: the
family is one body on `(r, c, k)`; from 52.5: its form is a quotient per
chart; from rule 17: a reader writes a coordinate or returns a demand. What
this chapter adds is the organ that stood between a scene and its form in
the parent tree and never crossed the fork: a 25×25 scene arriving at
extraction as one form of 712 vertices is not a cost to optimise but the
absence of a cut. 948 of the 1 120 corpus tasks have a side that was above
the parent's floor; 850 present a uniform separator row or column in every
input; 102 are integer frame ratios on every pair. The Stage 16 gap reads
differently under this: fifteen per cent of a 25×25 scene is a form that
cannot close, and fifteen per cent of one 4×5 chart of it can.

### 53.1 The scene cover

A scene is covered by charts under a reading before it is perceived as one
form. A **chart** is the atlas's chart (the vocabulary, NM1): one local
view of the cover with a transition on every overlap; on the substrate
it is NAMED by its support written out (A21, `pieces::piece_key`, since removed) —
coordinates of which every prefix is a coarser stratum, and never a
bounding box carried past the sensor boundary (law 11, checklist (f′)).
The support names the chart; it is not the chart. A **cover** is a `Keyed` of charts under
one reading. The family is then the ordinary family of each chart — the
train inputs and outputs restricted to it, frame by frame — extracted as
52.5 extracts any family, and the charts' forms are recomposed on the Čech
complex of the cover by the alternating coboundary (13.9, `cech::`), which
is the recomposition and needs no written map.

**The recursion ends at an identity of coordinates.** A chart is itself a
scene and is covered again; the recursion ends where the cover's key is the
scene's own key, one chart equal to the whole. There is no floor and no
constant: `FRAGMENT_FLOOR = 9` is refused by rule 5 and is not replaced by
a count of charts (rule 2). The routing floor — how much of a scene one
voice takes — is the voice's drawable room (23.8) and is read from the
book, never from the geometry.

**No reading is chosen by the engine** (rules 4, 15, review discipline for
the code). Every reading of the roster is tried in roster order; every cover
that closes is kept; covers that close and are incomparable are held as a
vortex until a court replay, a perception, or a mind's stated order collapses
them (Concordance 1.10). The first cover that addresses a demand is a choice
by arrival and is refused.

### 53.2 The readings

A **reading** is a way the sensor plane is cut into charts: Bands (the
uniform separator rows and columns every input carries), Components,
Lines, RingShells, PeriodCells (the spectrum cut, integer frame ratios),
HueStrata. The roster is governed as the letters are (law 6 as amended):
fixed, grown only by a court receipt on a probe — a reading whose first
cover on the corpus closes a family no other reading closes — and never by
a voice or a commit. Bands enters first because it is deducible in one
pass over the inputs; each further reading enters behind its own receipt.

**A reading has its own coordinate system, and a chart is named in it**
(ruled 2026-09-19, on the corpus reading that a separator shared by every
input of a family cuts 156 of 1 000 tasks while 566 tasks have inputs of
differing frames and no shared site set at all). Bands is read **per
frame**: each input's own separator rows and columns are its band
lattice, and a chart is named by its coordinate in that lattice — its band
index along `r` and along `c` — never by its support. The support at a
frame is the section that coordinate reads there (51.4: the fibre's unit
is the section), so charts correspond across frames by coordinate and
never by a search over supports, and a frame whose lattice does not reach
a coordinate holds that chart's fibre empty there: a section along `e₃`
(52.5 item 3), not a refusal. A family whose inputs carry no separator has
one chart under Bands, itself, and is cut by another reading or not at
all; `1d0a4b61` is such a family, and its cut is PeriodCells' or
Components' (K5), not Bands'.

### 53.3 A demand may name a stratum

50.5 gains one kind: `Demand::Chart { reading, chart, links }`, a chart
under a reading with no rule. It is keyed by (reading, chart key) and
deduplicated by that key, never by a count, so a hundred scenes blocked on
one chart class under one reading are one demand. It is the first demand
the registry may dispatch as a **sub-problem**: a voice that refuses a
chart hands it back as this demand; another mind may take it and the
market prices it (24.3, 42.6). The five algebraic kinds of 50.5 stand
unchanged; a `Demand::Chart` is spatial in the sense of a key on the
sensor's stratum and in no other.

### 53.4 The quantified citation

A `Glued` vertex cites a form **over a fibre** — every chart of a reading
on which the cited form closes — and its placement is re-derived at each
chart it is spoken on from that chart's own key and the cited form's
frame, never stored once for one placement (law 12). The single-placement
citation `Form::glue(s, addr, placement, magnitude)` is the degenerate case
of one chart, and the tape carries no per-chart placement. This is what
makes a chart's rule general enough to be worth extracting: one citation
speaks every chart of a banded scene.

### 53.6 A form's vertices are its charts, never its pieces (ruled 2026-09-19)

A 25×25
scene of three frames arriving as a form of 2 899 vertices, 12 011 faces
and 971 loops is not a large form, it is an enumeration of the scene's
bodies held in a form's carriers, and every reader that walks it is
brute force by construction. Nothing a perception produces may be
proportional to the laminae or the pieces of a scene; it is proportional
to the scene's charts.

A form's word vertices are the quotients of its charts (52.5 item 2), one
per transport class acting on the charts it acts on, and its demand
vertices are one per (kind, chart) (50.5). A cover's pieces are not
vertices of the family's form. A cover is what one chart's quotient
refused, and it is carried as **one vertex per cover** — the deformation
on that chart — whose nerve, meets and filed classes are the cover's own
content, held below that vertex in the chart's fibre and reached by key
when the form is spoken or replayed. The orbits the form walks are the
orbits among its charts; the orbits among a cover's pieces are classified
once inside the cover and filed as torsion on the cover's vertex (50.8
case 3), never lifted to the form. Pieces correspond across frames by the
chart coordinate along `e₃` (51.3, 52.5 reading 1), so a piece at frame k
and its image at frame k+1 are one fibre, not two vertices.

**The carrier is unchanged and the tape is unbroken.** A `Vertex::Word`
already is what this section names: one transport class, acting on the
charts it acts on through its `acts` fibre, one member per chart (D7).
The ruling lands in the percept and nowhere else: a cover's carried pieces
are grouped by transport class exactly as a chart's quotients are, one
Word vertex per class with one member per chart the class carries a piece
on; a chart on which one class carries two pieces by two different
carriages is 50.5's multiplicity, a `Source` demand on that chart, never
two vertices and never two members; the cover's meets are faces between
those members through the incidence the form already builds on supports;
the orbits among pieces are classified inside the cover and filed as
torsion by class, where the form already files them. No vertex kind, no
tape field and no address of an unchanged form moves; the version byte
stays K3's.

The bound is therefore structural and is written as a test, not a limit:
the number of word vertices of a form does not exceed the number of
charts of the scene times the number of readings that cut it, plus one
vertex per cover and one per demand kind and chart. On `1d0a4b61` that is
tens, and a form of thousands is refused by the claim. This is P7's
ruling 1 landed at the form rather than at the index, and it is what the
cut of 53.1 cuts.

## 54. The derivation of a coordinate and its inverse (ruled 2026-09-20)

Ruled by design review under A21, M2, law 12 and Part IX, on the reading
that the genome on disk had become a trie keyed by addresses whose values
were tapes 68% made of those same addresses, with the derivation empty on
every voice — a structure that navigates a name in order to read the name
back, built because the key could not be inverted. M2's own invariant says
`decode(address)` re-derives the form; the tree never met it, and treated
the gap as a wall ("there is no decoder"). This chapter composes the
derivation the document already states across nine chapters into one
chain, names what the key was missing, and writes the inverse.

### 54.1 The chain, sensor to key

Every coordinate the engine holds is an output of one of these steps, and
nothing else is a coordinate (rule 17):

1. **Laminae.** The sensor reads `(r, c, k, h)`: row, column, frame, hue
   (51.3). The only place a pair of integers is a coordinate (law 11).
2. **Bodies.** One-hue 6-adjacent components on `(r, c, k)`; a body's shape
   and moduli from its harmonics (B2, 38.2); its chart is its moduli, an
   `Invariant`.
3. **The cover.** The scene's charts under a reading (53.1, 53.2), each
   named by its coordinate in the reading's own lattice.
4. **The quotient.** The versor carrying one body onto another, in closed
   form from the moments, the coset's geodesic (16.4, 50.2 step 1); the
   hue map read lamina by lamina.
5. **Canonical form.** The rotor in A1's form; the versor in A4's writing;
   the class vector as the blade decomposition of the holonomy (12.6).
6. **The word.** A22's peel of the rotor, factored through the presentation
   by A12 (50.2 step 2): the citations and the residue.
7. **The form.** One `Word` vertex per transport class on the charts it acts
   on (52.5, 53.6); faces between members by the incidence (21 step 2);
   orbits by 12.2; sections along `e₃`, each at its frame (51.4, 51.8);
   demands one per kind and chart (50.5).
8. **The key.** A21: the coordinates of 5 and 7 written in a fixed order,
   length-prefixed, a prefix a coarser stratum; the address is M2's
   composite of them.

### 54.2 What the key carries, and what is a receipt

The key carries the closed sub-complex whole, so that step 8 inverts to
step 7: for every vertex its kind, its rotor's A1 key, **every member's
chart** and that member's A4 carriage, contact and sorted gauge; for every
face its two ends, its word, and at every member pair the carriage, the
gauge and **the edge's value** as the transport it is; for every demand
its kind, its chart and **its remainder as that chain's own address**
(from_residual, A5); the ratio, the sections, each at its frame coordinates,
the opened axes. Nothing in it is a digest, a position or a count standing
for a property.

The key does not carry evidence, and evidence is a receipt (Part IX): the
derivation's citations — which generators a mind factored through — and
the certificates of the pivots a form rests on are receipts on the ledger,
keyed by the address they are evidence for, replayed by the court there
and never part of identity, because two minds reaching one vertex by two
derivations reach one address (1.5). The remainder chain is identity, not
evidence: it is what the form does not close.

### 54.3 The inverse

`Form::from_address` is A21's inverse and the only decoder: it reads the
key and re-derives the form's vertices, faces, orbits, sections, demands
and axes, with `orbits_of` run on the faces read (orbits are never written).
The A21 property `from_address(address(f)) ≡ f` — same vertices by
`same_vertex`, same faces by the faces' words and places, same sections and
demands — is a property test over generated forms, and it is the test of
this chapter.

### 54.4 Succession is a section, not a replay

What stands at frame `n` is `σ(n)`, read at the frame's own coordinate
from the sections the key carries and the members' frames (51.8); the
transition between frames `k` and `k + 1` is the connection the edge
carries along `e₃` (52.5 reading 6). No reader reconstructs a form by
walking frames in order, and no carrier stores the order in which a form
was built.

### 54.5 What retires

The form tape as a cognitive carrier: the genome on disk is the trie of
addresses (25 as ruled), and a word's value on disk is nothing, because
the key is the form; the tape survives only as the wire's frame for an
address plus its receipts (Part IX), and `FORM_TAPE_VERSION` is never bumped
for the form again. `from_element_form`, `as_element_form` and every reader
that decodes a tape to reach a form read `from_address`. Every address in
the tree changes once, when this chapter lands (§10).

### 54.6 Binding

```
src/transducer/sentence/chart.rs      form_vertex_key completed (54.2); Form::from_address (54.3)
src/transducer/sentence/address.rs    the form's tape retired from cognition; the wire frame carries the address and receipts (54.5)
src/transducer/element/vertex.rs      the demand's remainder as a chain address; the edge value written
src/court/verdict/replay.rs           citations and certificates as receipts keyed by address (54.2)
src/client/sdk/epigenome/             the genome as addresses; Held reads from_address (25, 54.5)
src/transducer/sentence/tests/properties.rs   from_address(address(f)) ≡ f
```

## 55. Phase, not place: why the 2-skeleton was empty (ruled 2026-09-22)

### 55.1 The reading

Four constructions were tried for the witness that certifies a 2-simplex,
and all four returned zero:

```
an l1 stencil  |dr| + |dc| = 1     a coordinate metric imposed on raw input
the open star  St(B) = B u dB      a neighbourhood synthesised from a partition
Khalimsky      corners at (2r,2c)  a square raster and its 4-neighbour corner
the spectral   shared cyclotomic l  phase, not place
```

The first three are the same fiat in better clothing: each asks whether
three charts contain a mutual POINT, and each must reintroduce a lattice
to answer. A lattice is a cage. The fourth is not a cage and it still
returned zero, because the quantity it measures is identically trivial.

The corpus's 186 meets read:

```
phase:   N finite, 0 infinite, 0 unread, every count in period slot 1
nerve:   charts over cells, 0 shared by two or more in 9 of 10 forms
defects: trivial 0 elliptic 0 hyperbolic N parabolic 0 non-simple 0
cycles:  vacuum 64 resonant 0, over 1458 charged steps of 1777
```

`l = 1` is `R ~ +-1`. Of the three sectors of `Spin+(3,1)` the corpus
occupies exactly one:

```
elliptic / compact K      l = 1 on all 186     ABSENT
parabolic / null  L^2 = 0 parabolic 0          ABSENT
hyperbolic / exp(p)       186 meets, mu > 0    THE WHOLE CORPUS
```

Every negative reading of the session is that single fact reported four
ways. The 2-skeleton is not missing because the nerve builder, the codec
or the coboundary logic is wrong.

### 55.2 The scalar collapse that forced it

`54.7`'s quantum was `M = 1 + sum |p_i - P|^2`, defended as "a moment, not
an extent: every cell enters symmetrically and no axis is privileged, so
there is no box". Privileging no axis was the defect. The second moment is
a TENSOR and this stores its TRACE:

```
M2  = sum (p - P) (x) (p - P)          in Sym2(Q), carries orientation
Tr M2 = sum |p_i - P|^2                 invariant under every rotation
```

`Tr M2` is an `SO(2)` invariant, so it treats every chart as an ISOTROPIC
POINT MASS. Two isotropic point masses have no relative frame angle; the
only relation between them is the geodesic through the masses' centres, and

```
R = 1 - v_b v_a,  B = v_a ^ v_b,  B^2 = sinh^2 d >= 0  =>  pure boost, l = 1
```

It was algebraically impossible for bare centres of mass to yield anything
but `l = 1`. The collapse is doubled: `|p_i - P|^2` sums the axes per
cell, then `sum` sums the cells. A single rational cannot orient anything.

This is the same defect already ruled on at `bivector_squares` — "is the
scalar collapsing the content into a single plane" — committed a second
time in a new place.

### 55.3 Relative orientation, exactly, without eigendecomposition

Diagonalising an isolated `M2` needs the roots of its characteristic
quadratic, which lie in `Q(sqrt D)`: refused by law 4 and rule 11 —
exactness (re-cited 2026-10-08, the 1.10 audit: the ground is that the roots
are not rational, a law of the mathematics, never rule 4). The RELATIVE frame
does not need either matrix diagonalised. Split off the isotropic part:

```
M2 = (1/2) Tr(M2) I + D,   D traceless, symmetric

u = ((M_rr - M_cc)/2) e1 + M_rc e2      the deviatoric bivector, in Q^2
```

A rank-2 symmetric tensor rotates at DOUBLE the shape's angle, `u_b =
R(2phi) u_a`. For congruent shapes the anisotropic magnitudes agree, and
the double angle is fixed in `Q` with no root taken:

```
Delta       = ((M_rr - M_cc)/2)^2 + M_rc^2      = |u_a|^2 = |u_b|^2
cos 2phi    = (u_a . u_b) / Delta   in Q
sin 2phi    = (u_a ^ u_b) / Delta   in Q
```

### 55.4 The grid group's projective rotors carry no roots

Congruent shapes on a discrete base are related by `D4`, so
`phi in {0, pi/2, pi, 3pi/2}` and `2phi in {0, pi, 2pi, 3pi}`, on which
`cos 2phi` and `sin 2phi` take values in `{-1, 0, 1}` only. The half-angle
rotors are rational as PROJECTIVE versors — a versor is projective, so the
`1/sqrt 2` never has to be written:

```
phi     rotor                  projective versor   mu = <R>0^2/<R~R>0 - 1   l
0       1                      1                   1/1 - 1 =  0             1
90      (1 + e12)/sqrt 2       1 + e12             1/2 - 1 = -1/2           4
180     e12                    e12                 0/1 - 1 = -1             2
270     (-1 + e12)/sqrt 2      -1 + e12            1/2 - 1 = -1/2           4
```

`(1 + e12)(1 - e12) = 1 - e12^2 = 2 in Q`. A 90° turn is minted
exactly when `u_a . u_b = -Delta` and `u_a ^ u_b = 0`.

### 55.5 Where the frame is discarded

`meet_edge` is handed `va, vb` and uses them only for `hue_at` (the gauge
lane). Its carriage is OVERWRITTEN:

```
edge_of:    Transport { word, carriage: d.geo(&t), gauge }   d, t peeled from gamma
meet_edge:  edge.carriage = r                                r = 1 - v_b v_a
```

`frame_base_point(s)` maps a versor to a POINT `V v0 V~`, and a point has
no orientation, so the overwrite replaces a carriage carrying gamma's own
dilator and transvection with one built from two orientation-free centres.
The comment's hedge names it: "edge_of's own carriage stands" — only on
the refusal path.

The WORD survives the overwrite, peeled from `gamma = s_b s_a^-1`, so
`l = 1` on the word is a fact about the corpus (the carried pieces are
rotationally aligned) and NOT a consequence of the transvection formula.
The two halves must not be conflated: the formula constrains the carriage,
the measurement was on the word.

TWO REPAIRS COLLIDED AND THE SECOND KILLED THE FIRST. `edge_of` was
repaired under 54.7 R3 to stop reading `translator_of(gamma)` — the
conformal motor whose `e_inf` generator is null, forcing `I1 = 0` and
synthesising the four parabolic/undecomposed cycles — and to read
`transvection_of(gamma)` instead. From that moment `edge_of` emitted an
authentic intrinsic connection and the `meet_edge` overwrite stopped
being a fix. It became a regression: discarding gamma's dilator `d`,
discarding gamma's transvection `t`, and substituting a central-force
chord between unoriented centres. The hedge "edge_of's own carriage
stands" says it exactly — the correct code ran only on the failure path.

AND IT MADE THE NON-SIMPLE SECTOR UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, by the
same identity 54.7 states about `basepoint_transvection`:

```
<R>2 = v_a ^ v_b,  a simple blade
(v_a ^ v_b) ^ (v_a ^ v_b) = 0  =>  I2 = <Omega ^ Omega>4 = 0
```

So no cycle of pure chords could carry a screw, whatever the scene did.
The theorem was proved at one site and left standing at another, where
this ruling had installed it.

Removing the overwrite and leaving `edge_of`'s carriage, the corpus reads:

```
clobbered   defects: ... hyperbolic N parabolic 0 non-simple 0
gamma-derived defects: ... hyperbolic N parabolic 0 non-simple 3
edges asked: measured N, unspelled 0, unread 0, not rigid 0
```

`non-simple 0 -> 3`: three genuine loxodromic screws — a transvection
along an axis coupled to a twist about that same axis — were being
erased. 54.7's conclusion that the four non-simple readings "did NOT

A PREDICTION OF THIS RULING THAT FAILED. Removing the overwrite was
expected to expose `transvection_of`'s Cayley pole at `|u|^2 = 1`, the
same pole 54.7 found in `basepoint_transvection`, and to refuse every

`displacement_of` yields general rationals, and the rational unit sphere
is measure zero among them. The pole is still there and is still a defect
at that site — it simply is not reached by this corpus.

The full connection couples the two:

```
g_ab = theta_b (1 - v_b v_a) theta_a^-1
```

spacelike ^ spacelike twist against timelike ^ timelike shear, which is
the whole `Spin+(3,1)` versor rather than one sector of it.

An authored generator is not a derivation. `McFarland_2026_v5_2` section

## 56. The axiom register (ruled 2026-09-22)

Axioms A.1-A.10 are `ipsal-autic`'s, whose register marks A.1-A.4 as
carried forward unchanged from the convergence-engine and A.5-A.10 as its
own. They are NOT adopted wholesale: three are refused, and the refusals
matter more than the imports because each would flatten something this
engine measures. A.11 is native to this register.

### 56.1 Imported

```
A.6   DIMENSIONAL COMPLETENESS, UNBOUND. Every contradiction admits a
      higher-dimensional resolution. A.6 names a MECHANISM (escalation),
      never a bound. The `ipsal-autic` audit (#126) had to split it from the value
      N = 11 after the two were conflated — mechanism read as constant,
      which is the error class of `Fill::Open` standing for absence.
      Here: the ascend pivot, and T21(iii)'s "a dimension is never
      declared, it is paid for".

A.8   TORSIONAL PERSISTENCE. Torsion is never destroyed. It is promoted,
      annihilated against an opposing pair, or deposited as an inverse
      record; total information is monotonically NON-DECREASING.
      Here: drain's conservation law, which 55 had no invariant for. It
      is stronger than a Lyapunov bound — strain cannot be relaxed away
      at all, only moved or recorded, so a drain that lowers `sum mu`
      without exhibiting a partner or a deposit is refused.

A.9   METRIC AUTONOMY. Each entity computes its own local coherence
      metric. There is no global metric, and two entities may assign
      different values to one state without contradiction.
      Here: the form-scoped quantum is correct BY AXIOM, not by the
      argument 54.7 reached for. A per-chord metric would still be wrong
      — the autonomy is the entity's, and a form is the entity.

A.10  SYMBIOTIC CO-DIMENSIONALITY. Two manifolds of differing
      dimensionality may occupy the same spatial references without
      collapse IF AND ONLY IF the manifolds' interface is governed by a luminal
      phase gradient. The tether is a shared boundary in the
      cohomological sense, not a pointer or a channel.
      Here: the meets are tethers. And the gradient must be LUMINAL —
      null, `L² = 0` — because on a null boundary the induced metric is
      degenerate and the two interiors do not crush each other. This engine's runs
      between `v² = -1` points: timelike, `mu > 0`. Naming it luminal was
      an error (55.7).
```

### 56.2 Refused, and why each would flatten

```
A.4   RATIONAL INNER PRODUCT, "symmetric, bilinear, POSITIVE-DEFINITE".
      False here. `Cl(4,1)` is indefinite, `e_-^2 = -1`, and the
      hyperboloid sheet is `-t^2 + x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = -1`. Positive
      definiteness would flatten every boost generator into an elliptic

A.7   HOLONOMIC INVARIANT as written — closure in `H^1(X, Z)`, "closed
      paths always return to the topological starting class modulo

A.6-bind-11   N = 11 EXACTLY, sourced to an architecture document. The `ipsal-autic`
      register is honest that it is a constitutional BINDING and not a
      theorem of the algebra. A hardcoded generator is refused whatever
      register it arrives in.
```

### 56.3 A.11 — Harmonic multipole completeness (native to this register)

STATEMENT. The geometric state of a discrete spatial chart is completely
and irreducibly characterised by its ascending harmonic multipoles in `Q`.
No higher-rank moment may be collapsed into a lower-rank scalar trace
before the frame is evaluated.

```
RADIAL SECTOR (scalar)       tr(M2) = Ixx + Iyy
  governs isotropic dilation and the basepoint's radius on the sheet.
  CARRIES ZERO ORIENTATIONAL AUTHORITY.

ORIENTATION SECTOR (tensor)  the irreducible traceless harmonics
  2nd harmonic, turns at 2phi:  D = M2 - (1/2) tr(M2) I,
                                u = ((Ixx - Iyy)/2) e1 + Ixy e2
                                orients an asymmetric body.
  4th harmonic, turns at 4phi:  h4 = (h4x, h4y)
                                orients a body whose M2 is ISOTROPIC —
                                a square, a cross — which the second
                                moment cannot tell from a disc.

SINGLE PRODUCER (law 12)     the multipoles are computed ONCE, at
  `blade::lift`, as exact rational invariants of the support. No
  downstream consumer may recompute them, approximate them, or substitute
  a scalar surrogate.
```

WHY IT IS AN AXIOM AND NOT A CONVENTION. `tr(M2)` is an `SO(2)`
invariant. A chart read through its trace alone is an ISOTROPIC POINT
MASS; two point masses have no relative angle; the only relation left is
the geodesic through the masses' centres, whose bivector is a simple blade with
`I2 = 0` and `l = 1`. The collapse does not lose precision, it loses a
SECTOR — and it does so silently, reporting `l = 1` as a measurement of
the scene rather than as an artefact of the reading.

`(u + iv)^4` transforms as `e^(i4phi)(u + iv)^4`, which is why `h4` turns
at `4phi` and resolves the `45°` ambiguity `D` is blind to. For an
isotropic disc `h4 = 0`; for a discrete square it does not vanish.

WHAT IT FORBIDS, by name. 54.7's `M = 1 + sum |p_i - P|^2` — a doubled
collapse (axes summed per cell, then cells summed) AND a shadow producer
of a trace `blade::lift` already computes as `r2 = (ixx + iyy)/n`. The
architecture was already right: trace for scale, tensor for orientation.

### 56.4 What is already in hand

```
Blade.inertia  [Q; 6]   (Ixx, Iyy, Ixy, Izz, Ixz, Iyz), about the centroid,
                        exact, rotation-covariant, no eigen and no roots,
                        parallel-axis at every order (each lamina carries
                        the unit square's own 1/12 on the plane axes)
Blade.quartic  [Q; 3]   the isotropic part and the fourth harmonic
blade::deviatoric            u, or None for an isotropic body
blade::quartic_harmonic      h4, or None for a body with no orientation
blade::relative_double_angle (cos 2phi, sin 2phi) in Q, or None where the
                             two anisotropies differ — non-congruent
                             bodies have no rotation between them
```

THE MOD-PI RESIDUE. A rank-2 symmetric tensor is invariant under a half
turn, so `u` fixes `phi` only mod `pi`: `phi = 0` and `phi = pi` both give
`2phi = 0`, while the rotors `1` and `e12` of the two are not projectively equal.
`relative_double_angle` therefore returns the angle and does NOT mint a
rotor from it. The residue is a question about the SUPPORT and is settled
by carrying a candidate through `versor_coset_ordered`, which tests it
against the sites rather than guessing.

### 56.5 The connection, framed

```
g_ab = theta_b . gamma . theta_a^-1
```

`gamma = s_b s_a^-1` carries the metric displacement between basepoints,
restored in 55.5 by deleting the chord overwrite. `theta` carries the
orientation, solved from `D_a -> D_b`, or from `h4_a -> h4_b` where
`||D|| = 0`. Spacelike-wedge-spacelike twist against
timelike-wedge-timelike shear: the whole `Spin+(3,1)` versor rather than
one sector of it, and the route by which a word can carry `l in {2, 4}`.

                                 relative_double_angle (blade/frame.rs) read them

## 57. Corrections from the A.11 landing (ruled 2026-09-22)

The landing of A.11 overturned three readings this doctrine had already
recorded.
They are corrected here rather than edited in place: the wrong reading and
what unseated it are both part of the record.

### 57.1 "The cover is a partition" is WITHDRAWN

55.1 read `charts over cells, 0 shared by two or more` in nine of ten
forms and concluded the cover is a partition whose nerve is a set of
isolated points. That measured `da`/`db` from `cover.carried`, which held
ONLY THE CODOMAIN — where each piece landed.

The codebase already said what that reading gives. `Supports`:

```
Both, because the nerve reads meets on both. A deformation is a map OUT
OF the input, so the Cech nerve is the nerve of the cover of the SOURCE:
two carriages sharing a domain overlap on the whole of it, however far
apart the carriages' codomains land. That is the replication case, and the only
case in which the transition between two copies of one shape is visible
at all. Meets on the codomain are the merge case. READING ONLY THE
CODOMAIN LEAVES THE NERVE DISCRETE.
```

The nerve is of PULLBACKS, not pushouts. Two carriages that read the same
source overlap on the whole of it and land wherever they land; looking at
the landings shows disjoint interiors by construction and says nothing.
`0 certified triples` was therefore a property of which half was stored,
reported as a property of the corpus.

`CarriedPiece` now holds `Supports { domain, codomain }`. The nerve
measurement still reads the codomain and is still wrong; correcting it is
open work, not a landed result.

CORRECTED IN 58.1, AND THE EXPECTATION ABOVE IS REFUSED BY THE READING.
The nerve now reads the source. `0 certified triples` holds on BOTH halves
over 252 forms, and the source shares LESS than the image, not more. The
2-skeleton is empty as a property of this corpus's decomposition, which is
what 55.1 concluded; the reason 55.1 gave for it, and the reason this
section gave for withdrawing it, are both wrong.

### 57.2 Congruence was the wrong group

56.4 gave `relative_rotor` a congruence gate — equal cell counts, equal
`||u||^2`. The carriage carries a DILATOR, so a 2x domino is 8 cells
against 2 and was refused though its rotation is perfectly defined and is
the identity. A transformation here is a transvection transmutation
through transduction, not a rigid motion; isometry was too small a group
and similarity is the right one.

The scale-free form takes no roots. Under `u -> s^4 u` with `s^4 > 0`
every sign survives, so

```
sgn(u_a . u_b)   = sgn(cos 2phi)
sgn(u_a ^ u_b)   = sgn(sin 2phi)
```

decide which of the four turns applies and `cos 2phi` is never formed.
Relaxing the gate on `relative_double_angle` INSTEAD would not loosen it
but break it: `(u_a.u_b)/||u_a||^2` with unequal norms is `s^4 cos 2phi`,
which can exceed +-1 and is not an angle. The two readings sit on
different layers and are not rivals:

```
METRIC      relative_double_angle   O(2); needs ||u_a||^2 = ||u_b||^2;
                                    answers an exact direction cosine
PROJECTIVE  relative_rotor          Spin(2)/Z2 on P^1(Q); a similitude
                                    invariant; never forms cos 2phi
```

One is the metric restriction of the other's projective ray action.

### 57.3 The 180° turn is a parity theorem

56.4 called the mod-`pi` residue something to resolve later. It cannot be
resolved by the harmonics at all. `u` and `h4` are EVEN-rank moments —
`(-x)^2 = x^2`, `(-x)^4 = x^4` — so `u(-x) = u(x)` and no even moment
distinguishes `phi` from `phi + pi`. Closing it locally needs an ODD
invariant: a third harmonic, or a directed boundary contour.

Where cardinalities match the cells settle it. Where they differ — a
transmuted carry — nothing local can, and `Frame::HalfOpen` (since removed) carries the
representative together with the fact that it is a projective class.

PICKING A SIGN PER EDGE IS NOT A SHORTCUT, IT IS A FABRICATION. Three
edges of a cycle guessed independently manufacture a `-1` holonomy out of
nothing and the complex reports an obstruction it invented. Left open,
each edge holds a `Z2` gauge freedom and the COBOUNDARY arbitrates: `d
sigma` fixes the signs globally where a 2-cell locks, and where it does
not the obstruction is real.

### 57.4 The Cayley pole is the light cone

`transvection_of` builds `B = u ^ e_-`, `B^2 = |u|^2`, so `1 - B^2`
vanishes on the unit sphere. That is geometry, not arithmetic:

```
cosh theta = (1 + |u|^2)/(1 - |u|^2),     |u| = tanh(theta/2)
```

`|u| -> 1` is `theta -> infinity`. The chart covers every FINITE boost and
its boundary is infinite rapidity. No repair removes it.

What was wrong is that the boundary refused ANONYMOUSLY, falling into
`EdgeRefusal::NoReading`, where a displacement at the cone read the same
as a versor that could not be parsed. It is now named where it is
crossed. And it is the second half of `parabolic 0`: the luminal sector
is not merely unbuilt (55.7) — it is ACTIVELY REFUSED here whenever a
displacement reaches it. Building Layer 2 means giving this boundary a
READING rather than a refusal.

### 57.5 What the frame measured

With `g_ab = (theta_b . theta_a^-1) . gamma` wired on both sides:

```
frames: 184 framed, 2 half-open, 0 UNFRAMED
phase:  periods [0, 48, 0, ...] - every word still l = 1
defects: non-simple 3, unchanged
```

The frame computes on every one of the 186 meets and the words stay at
`l = 1`, so `theta_b theta_a^-1 = 1` throughout: the carried pieces of
this corpus either never turn or all turn alike. `0 unframed` is what
makes that trustworthy — no silent refusal hides a turn. Before this the
two were indistinguishable and `l = 1` was reported as a fact about the
scene when nothing had asked it.

## 58. The nerve on the pullback, and the cover's three addresses (ruled 2026-09-22)

57.1 withdrew "the cover is a partition" on the ground that the reading had
measured the CODOMAIN — where each piece landed — while the Cech nerve of a
deformation belongs on the SOURCE. The reading has now been taken on the
source. The conclusion survives; the reason for it does not.

### 58.1 A1 — the reading, on both halves

`certified_triples` is re-targeted to `supports.domain`, read per cover,
with the charts NOT deduplicated by footprint: two carriages over one
source region are two SECTIONS of that region's fibre, `g_ij = theta_j
theta_i^-1 . gamma_ij`, and folding them to one chart erases exactly the
holonomy a 2-cell would carry. A cover is INDEXED by carriage and the nerve
of an indexed cover admits repeats.

The image reading is taken on the same walk, so "the codomain is a
partition" is a measurement rather than a recollection.

Over 252 family forms — the seven tests of `family::tests::retract`, four
of them corpus-wide, 36 corpus forms at the lift:

```
nerve/source   245 forms  0 shared by two or more      0 certified triples
                 7 forms  2 shared by two or more      0 certified triples
nerve/image    245 forms  0 shared                     0 triples
                 7 forms  8 shared                     0 triples
```

`0 certified triples` on 252 of 252, on BOTH halves. No cell of either base
stands in three charts, so there is no 2-simplex to certify and none is
invented (rule 11). The reading is not vacuous: `cech::tests::nerve`
carries the positive case, `read_nerve_shared_element_certifies_one_two_cell`.

### 58.2 What that overturns, and what it leaves standing

THE CONCLUSION OF 55.1 STANDS. The 2-skeleton is empty, and it is empty as
a property of this corpus's decomposition rather than of which half was
stored. 57.1's expectation — that the domain would show the replication the
codomain cannot — is REFUSED by the measurement.

THE EXPECTED ASYMMETRY IS THE OTHER WAY ROUND. The source shares LESS than
the image, on the same seven forms: 2 cells against 8. Replication (one
domain carried by several versors) does not occur in this corpus; merging
(several domains reaching one codomain) does, slightly.

AND THE CODOMAIN IS NOT A STRICT PARTITION. `int(B'_i) ^ int(B'_j) = {}`
was asserted "by construction" and is false on seven forms. A cover piece's
codomain is an ASSEMBLY — one output piece in the pullback, a set of them
in the propagation — and two assemblies can share a member. The peels are
under no obligation to agree on granularity, which is the whole of 50.8,
and that is where the shared cells come from.

WHY THE SOURCE IS THIN. `pieces_of` takes one-hue 6-connected components,
and the pullback assembles WHOLE pieces. Two preimages therefore overlap
only where one input piece lies under two output pieces. In this corpus
`charts` is close to `cells` on most forms — 33 charts over 33 cells, 36
over 38 — so the pieces are near-singletons and there is nothing to share.

### 58.3 The 1-cells and the 2-cells are read on two different covers

THIS IS OPEN AND IS NOT ACTED ON HERE. The cover's meet index is built over
`support UNION ring_of_support(support)` — a site one 4-step out counts as
an occupant — so the 1-simplices of the nerve come from a THICKENED cover.
The 2-simplices are certified over the bare support. Two covers, one nerve:
by law 12 that is two producers of one fact, and the simplex dimension
decides which one answers.

Either both dimensions read the thickened cover or neither does. The ring
is a lattice stencil, which is what the standing constraint on rigid
lattices refuses, so this wants a ruling and not a patch. It is recorded
here because it is the one structural reason a 2-cell could exist over this
corpus and does not.

### 58.4 E8 — the cover's three addresses are coordinates

`family::pieces` wrote a piece, a carriage and a meet, each out of its own
content and every carrier holding one was `Keyed<V, Any>`: loose bytes that
could not tell one from another. They are declared — `coord::Piece`,
`coord::Carriage`, `coord::Meet`, tags 20 to 22 — each invertible, and
`pieces_of`, `Cover::carried`, `Cover::meets`, `Cover::refused`,
`Pending::placed`, `Pending::consumed` and `cover_vertex` take the
coordinate rather than bytes.

ONE DEFECT SURFACED IN THE DECLARING. `assembly_key` wrote a ONE-PIECE
assembly as that piece's bare address and a many-piece one as a run of
length-prefixed pieces, so the bytes did not say which they were and
nothing could read a carriage address back at all. The collapse existed
only so the pullback — which assembles a domain and names one output piece
— and the propagation — which names one input piece and assembles an image
— would agree on the address of a carriage between two whole pieces. A
`coord::Carriage` carries a LIST on both sides and the two passes agree
because both sides are lists, not because one collapses into the other's
shape.

A key this reader wrote and cannot read back is a defect and not a reading
of the corpus, so `CoverTally::undecodable` (since removed) counts it apart from every
"nothing was there" beside it.

### 58.5 The frame axis was named the hue

`coord::Lamina` (since removed) named its third axis `hue` and every caller fed it
`support_of`'s third component, which is `Lamina`'s `k`: the corpus's own
`e_3`, 51.3's sixth adjacency direction, the axis `at_frame_zero`
recentres. The colour never reached that coordinate and could not — a cover
piece is of ONE hue by construction and carries it on `coord::Piece` — so
the base a cover is read over is three SPATIAL axes and the palette is a
coordinate of the chart. The bytes are unchanged; the key now says what it
always spelled.

## 59. Contact is tension, not coincidence (ruled 2026-09-22)

58.3 purged `ring_of_support` from the cover's meet index on the ruling that
neither dimension of a nerve may read a stencil. The reading that followed
is the largest correction of this period, and it opens the bridge
between the harmonic layer and the luminal one.

### 59.1 What the purge measured

```
                       with the stencil          bare supports
meets                  186                       2
   carried an edge     186                       2
chords                 186                       2
geodesic / off-sheet   186 / 0                   2 / 0
frames                 184 framed 2 half-open    0 framed 2 half-open 0 unframed
forms carrying an orbit  14                        2
lib suite              510 s                     289 s
```

184 of 186 meets were raster artifacts. The two survivors are the two that
were already `Frame::HalfOpen`.

57.5 IS OVERTURNED. It read "the frame computes on every one of the 186
meets and the words stay at `l = 1`, so `theta_b theta_a^-1 = 1`
throughout", and called `0 unframed` the reading that made it trustworthy.
Every one of those 184 framed meets was between two raster-adjacent
DISJOINT bodies under one global transformation — the `phi_2 phi_1^-1 = 1`
case exactly — so the frame was reading the identity off pairs that never
touched. `l = 1` was the stencil's signature and not a fact about the
corpus. The corpus's real content is ZERO determined relative frames and
TWO projective 180° turns.

A SECOND READING CAME FREE. The lib suite fell from 510 s to 289 s: nearly
half of it was occupancy entries and meets manufactured by dilation. That
also retires the performance question the typed coordinates were suspected
of — there was no regression; the stencil was the cost.

AND A CONSTANT DECAYED SILENTLY. `tests/cover.rs` carried `STROKE = 4`,
"the smallest stroke on this fixture that both needs more than one and
reaches the end". A site that yields a meet costs a read, so purging the
stencil made the cover cheaper and four reads then covered the whole
deformation in ONE stroke: the test asserted a resume it no longer forced.
A number calibrated against a cost is a second carrier of that cost (law
12). It is now the run's own measured `spend - 1`.

### 59.2 `R R~ = 4(1 + mu)`, and why contact was unreachable

With `R = 1 - v_b v_a` the algebra gives, in BOTH charts,

```
    <R>_0   = 1 - v_a . v_b
    R R~    = 2(1 - v_a . v_b) = 4(1 + mu)
    mu      = <R>_0^2 / <R R~>_0 - 1 = (-v_a . v_b - 1)/2
```

On Axiom B's sheet `v^2 = -1`, `v_a . v_b = -cosh d`, so `mu = sinh^2(d/2)
>= 0` and `R R~ >= 4` with equality IFF THE TWO BASEPOINTS COINCIDE. In the
dual-sphere chart `s^2 = +1` the identical formula gives `R R~ = 4` at
EXACT TANGENCY and `R R~ < 4` on interpenetration.

So `R R~ >= 4`, recorded as a non-singularity result, is the CONTACT FLOOR
READ IN A CHART WHERE CONTACT IS UNREACHABLE. The engine has been measuring
chords whose floor is the tangency condition and could never recognise it,
because on the hyperboloid `mu = 0` means "same point" and not "touching".
That is the structural reason the stencil had to exist.

THE RESOLUTION IS NOT TO CHANGE AXIOM B. Transport between basepoints
belongs on `H^3` with `v^2 = -1`. Contact is a relation between the bodies'
SPHERES, `s^2 = +1`. Two pairings of two different objects, sharing one
algebraic identity.

### 59.3 The tether: the inversive strain, exactly, without a root

For bodies with centroid `P` and radius of gyration `r`, the inversive
distance is

```
    delta = -v_a . v_b = (||P_a - P_b||^2 - r_a^2 - r_b^2) / (2 r_a r_b)
```

external tangency `||dP|| = r_a + r_b` gives `delta = 1`; internal tangency
`||dP|| = |r_a - r_b|` gives `-1`; intersecting gives `|delta| < 1`. NOTE
THE MINUS ON THE RADII: a first statement of this carried `+ r_a^2 + r_b^2`
and does not reach 1 at tangency. Then

```
    mu(a,b) = (delta - 1)/2 = (||P_a - P_b||^2 - (r_a + r_b)^2) / (4 r_a r_b)
```

`mu < 0` overlap, `mu = 0` tangency, `mu > 0` separated.

MU IS NOT RATIONAL, AND THIS SHAPES THE IMPLEMENTATION. `Blade` carries
`radius2()` — `r^2`, exact — and the denominator needs `r_a r_b =
sqrt(r_a^2 r_b^2)`. Law 1 would refuse it as an inexact root on nearly
every body, so `mu` AS A VALUE can never be written down and must never be
put on the wire.

The predicate survives where the value does not. Carry

```
    N   = ||P_a - P_b||^2 - r_a^2 - r_b^2     in Q   (its sign is the side)
    D^2 = 4 r_a^2 r_b^2                        in Q   (D > 0 always)
```

Then `delta = N/D` and `delta <= 1  <=>  N <= 0 or N^2 <= D^2` — a sign test
and one rational comparison, no root anywhere. Ordering two strains is the
same move. Under `x -> lambda x`, `N -> lambda^2 N` and `D^2 -> lambda^4
D^2`, so `delta^2 = N^2/D^2` is scale-free exactly.

### 59.4 Exact tangency is measure-zero; the sector is a coordinate

`mu = 0` is `||dP||^2 = (r_a + r_b)^2`, a rational locus of measure zero —
the same argument that made the Cayley pole never fire when the chord
clobber came off (`unspelled 0, unread 0`, because the rational unit sphere
is measure-zero). A hard threshold `mu_c = 0` would leave the 1-skeleton
exactly as empty as the purge left it. CONTACT IS A SECTOR, NEVER A LOCUS.

AND THE SECTOR MUST BE A COORDINATE. A sector that is only a PREDICATE has
to be evaluated on every pair — `C(N,2)`, which is the brute force the
standing constraint forbids. The set of spheres at fixed inversive distance
from a given sphere is a PENCIL, and a pencil is the orbit of a
one-parameter transvection subgroup `exp(tB)`, `B = e_i ^ e_-`. That is the
containment cylinder: an orbit coordinate, exact, non-Euclidean, and KEYED,
so "which bodies share this body's sector" is a keyed read and nothing is
enumerated.

### 59.5 Superposition, not probability; a kernel, not a prune

Law 1 strikes probabilities by name and nothing is scored, so a weighted
tether is the harness returning by the side door. But a quantum
superposition is NOT probabilistic: amplitudes are exact and the evolution
deterministic; probability enters only at measurement, by a rule imposed
from outside. Several tethers held at once as EXACT ALTERNATIVES WITH NO
WEIGHT is admissible; tethers carrying likelihoods are not.

The engine already has the shape. `Frame::HalfOpen` (since removed) carries a projective
class rather than a determined rotor — one genuine `Z_2` gauge freedom, one
qubit — and after the purge BOTH surviving meets are half-open, so the
entire real 1-skeleton of this corpus is currently in superposition and
nothing else.

PRUNING IS REFUSED. Generate candidates and remove those that do not fit is
generate-and-test, a search over the scene. The exact equivalent that is
not a search: `k` half-open edges give `2^k` sign assignments, and the
coboundary condition is LINEAR OVER `F_2`. Compute a KERNEL, which returns
every consistent assignment at once in `O(k^3)` with no candidate ever
generated. Trivial kernel means the obstruction is real and the 2-cell
refuses; otherwise the surviving assignments ARE the collapsed
superposition. 57.3 already says this in words — "the coboundary
arbitrates: `d sigma` fixes the signs globally where a 2-cell locks" — and
it has never been computed because there have never been enough real edges
to have a kernel.

### 59.6 The horizon is spellability, and it is mind-relative

A dialled `mu_c` is the `STROKE = 4` defect again: a number standing where a
derived quantity belongs. The non-arbitrary cut available from the algebra
is SPELLABILITY — the tether condenses where the chord's transvection is a
word the alphabet holds, finite order under `phi(l) <= 4`, and refuses where
it is not. That ties the metric sector to the rotor sector through the one
bound already ruled, and gives 37.7 work it has never had: a strain just
outside the horizon is a DEMAND FOR A GENERATOR, not a dropped edge.

AND SPELLABILITY IS PER MIND. `word_or_demand` and `derive_against` run
against that voice's own crystal, and the five Epigenomes differ by what
each has adjoined. So two ideas tether for a mind that holds the generator
and refuse for one that does not — the same exact geometry condensing
differently in each voice. The five will not agree on the 1-skeleton, and
that disagreement is content the court arbitrates rather than noise.

### 59.7 The bridge: harmonic, luminal and contact meet at `mu = 0`

```
    mu = -sin^2(theta/2) < 0    elliptic     compact; A.11's even multipoles at 2phi, 4phi
    mu = 0                      TWO things   trivial (B = 0) AND parabolic (B != 0, B^2 = 0)
    mu = +sinh^2(d/2)  > 0      hyperbolic   transvection, Burgers vector, solder form
```

For a null generator `Omega = 1 + B`, `Omega Omega~ = 1 - B^2 = 1` and
`<Omega>_0 = 1`, so `mu = 0` — IDENTICAL TO THE IDENTITY. That is why
`BivectorKind` carries a type byte, and why collapsing Trivial into
Parabolic "put every identity orbit in the same class as every dislocation".
The scalar charge cannot see the luminal sector at all.

What separates them is the second Casimir `I_2 = ||<B^2>_4||^2 / w^2`, and
`I_2 = 0` identically for any SIMPLE blade. `R = 1 - v_b v_a` has `<R>_2 =
v_a ^ v_b`, a wedge of two vectors, therefore simple. SO A TRANSVECTION
CHORD CAN NEVER BE LUMINAL. That is the reason Layer 2 is unbuildable from
chords, independent of the cone refusal in `transvection_of` (57.4), and it
is why the `non-simple 3` defects recovered when the clobber came off are
not a curiosity: they are the ONLY three places in the corpus where `I_2 !=
0`, and therefore the only luminal candidates that exist.

THE BRIDGE BETWEEN HARMONIC AND LUMINAL IS THE NON-SIMPLE SECTOR. Harmonic,
luminal and contact all arrive at `mu = 0`; what tells them apart is the
Casimir the chord is structurally incapable of carrying.

### 59.8 Axiom C — the projective discipline, and what it refuses

The question was whether to widen the scalars to `Z`, `R`, the irrationals
or `C`. The answer is no, and the reasons are load-bearing:

- `R` BREAKS THE SPINE. Equality in `R` is undecidable and comparison only
  semi-decidable, so admitting it reintroduces tolerance — the flattening
  the project exists to refuse. Law 1's "things are equal, or they are not"
  does not survive it.
- `C` DESTROYS THE TETRACHOTOMY. `I_1` classifies a bivector by the SIGN of
  a scalar, and sign is a property of an ORDERED field. `C` is not
  orderable: `B^2 = -1` and `B^2 = +1` differ by `B -> iB`, so elliptic and
  hyperbolic become conjugate cases of one thing and `mu`'s sign — the
  whole kinematic charge — evaporates.
- `Z` ADDS NOTHING. Law 11 already places `Z^2` as the sensor's substrate
  and forbids it as a carrier.

THE ENGINE ALREADY HAS A BOUNDED-DEGREE AXIOM AND NEVER SAID SO. The
crystallographic restriction `phi(l) <= 4` is exactly a bound on field
extension degree: a rotor of order `l` lives in `Q(zeta_l)`, of degree
`phi(l)` over `Q`, and orders 5, 10, 12 are degree-4 extensions. "Exact Q"
has always been shorthand for "exact, ordered, decidably comparable, of
bounded degree".

WHAT AXIOM C SHOULD SAY IS A NARROWING, NOT A WIDENING. Every time this
engine met an apparently irrational quantity the resolution was to stay
PROJECTIVE and never normalize: `relative_rotor` decides a turn from
`sgn(u_a . u_b)` and `sgn(u_a ^ u_b)` rather than forming `cos 2phi`;
`same_versor` is an exact rational ratio over `Q^x` with no tolerance;
`mu` is the same shape, and `(N, D^2)` is that discipline written out.

    AXIOM C (PROJECTIVE CLOSURE). No quantity is normalized. Every
    invariant is a ratio of homogeneous forms of equal degree, carried as
    its numerator and its denominator, and the ratio is never evaluated.
    Scalars are exact, ordered and decidably comparable; extensions of Q
    are admitted only at bounded degree, and the bound is the one the
    crystallographic restriction already fixes.

ONE QUESTION DECIDES WHETHER EVEN THAT IS NEEDED. The above holds if
tension is COMPARED. It fails if tension is SUMMED: an action `S = sum_e
mu(e)` minimized globally needs one field containing every
`sqrt(r_a^2 r_b^2)` in the scene, and the tower degree grows with the
number of distinct radii, unboundedly. If condensation is instead a LOCAL
threshold per tether and a LOCAL holonomy test per membrane, nothing is
ever summed, everything stays in `Q`, and the ground state is reached by
relaxation rather than by evaluating a global scalar — which is also the
only one of the two that is not a search over the scene.

59 established that contact is tension and that the horizon is
spellability. Spellability is per mind, and that turns the 1-skeleton from
a property of the scene into a property of the observer.

### 60.1 Perception is the alphabet

Moved to [MU-CLIENT.md](MU-CLIENT.md); see its Rulings index.

### 60.2 The five voices do not share a 1-skeleton

Moved to [MU-CLIENT.md](MU-CLIENT.md); see its Rulings index.

### 60.3 The court arbitrates by adjunction, not by vote

Five different 1-skeletons are not resolved by counting. A vote needs
scores and law 1 strikes them. The court is a TOPOLOGICAL ARBITRATION
LAYER, and every object it compares is an exact field:

```
    voice A presents  a closed 2-cell             (a resolved concept)
    voice B presents  an open boundary + a demand (a missing generator)
    the court asks    does A's generator satisfy B's demand exactly in Q?
```

Where it does, 37.7 adjoins the generator to B's Epigenome, B's topology
shifts, the tether condenses and the superposition collapses
deterministically. Disagreement between the voices is therefore CONTENT the
court consumes, not noise it averages.

### 60.4 Non-simplicity is born in the composition, never in either factor

59.7 found that a transvection chord can never be luminal because `<R>_2 =
v_a ^ v_b` is a wedge of two vectors and therefore simple. The composition
is where it can change. With `Theta = theta_b theta_a^-1` compact and
`gamma` the chord,

```
    <g>_4 = <Theta_2 gamma_2>_4 = Theta_2 ^ gamma_2
```

which is non-zero exactly when the ROTATION PLANE AND THE BOOST PLANE ARE
NOT COPLANAR — a screw. That is `[p, p] subset k`, Thomas precession, the
structure Cartan already forces on this group.

Two consequences. `I_2 != 0` REQUIRES THE FRAME: with `Theta = 1` the
composition is `gamma` and is simple, so a corpus reading `0 framed`
produces no luminal candidate at any interface. And the luminal sector is
reachable only through the harmonic one — the frame is not decoration on
the carriage, it is the sole source of the second Casimir.

### 60.5 THE SECOND STENCIL — the purge was not universal

Read after 58.3, and it is why the defect tetrachotomy did not move:

```
defects over the corpus, AFTER the cover's ring was purged
    trivial 0 elliptic 0 hyperbolic 6 parabolic 0 non-simple 3   on 10 forms
    trivial 0 elliptic 0 hyperbolic 3 parabolic 0 non-simple 0   on 11 forms
    trivial 0 elliptic 0 hyperbolic 0 parabolic 0 non-simple 0   on 13 forms
```

`non-simple 3` survives. It survives because THE COVER'S MEET INDEX IS NOT
THE ONLY PLACE A RING IS DILATED. `family/pairing.rs`, inside
`star_and_site_faces`, walks `ring_of_support(supp)` and relates every
member standing at a site one 4-step out. The form's own faces — and
therefore its orbits, its `b_1`, and every `orbit_defects` reading above —
are built on that dilation.

So the accounting is:

```
    cover.meets  -> chords            purged (58.3); 186 -> 2
    star_and_site_faces -> faces      STILL STENCILLED (pairing.rs)
        -> loops -> b_1, orbit_defects, hyperbolic, non-simple, the spectra
```

EVERY READING IN 59.1 EXCEPT THE MEET COUNTS IS STILL CONTAMINATED, by a
different stencil. Whether the three non-simple defects are genuine luminal
candidates or artifacts of a second dilation IS UNDETERMINED until
`pairing.rs` is purged too, and no claim about Layer 2 may rest on them
before that. `ring_of_support` has exactly two callers and one of them is
now a comment; the other is this.

### 60.5b T1 landed, and the collapse did not come (measured 2026-09-22)

`pairing.rs`'s third pass is deleted and `ring_of_support` with it. The
expectation on both sides of the ruling was that faces and orbits would
collapse as the meets did and that the three non-simple defects would
vanish. THEY DID NOT.

```
over the 36 corpus forms of the lift        before T1      after T1
faces (cover meets + star)                  128            118
scene orbits                                 2              2
defects, cumulative: hyperbolic             6              6
defects, cumulative: non-simple             3              3
meets / chords / frames / geodesic          unchanged      unchanged
```

T1 removed TEN FACES OF 128 and changed no loop and no defect. The
ring-built faces in this corpus were not closing cycles: the dramatic
collapse had already happened at 58.3, where the meets went 186 to 2 and
the forms carrying an orbit went 14 to 2, and what `pairing.rs` was adding on
top of that was a thin margin that bounded nothing.

SO THE THREE NON-SIMPLE DEFECTS ARE NOT STENCIL ARTIFACTS. They survive
both purges, they arise on the two genuine orbits the corpus still carries,
and they are the only places where `I_2 != 0`. 60.5's own caveat — "no
claim about Layer 2 may rest on them before that" — is now discharged in
the candidates' favour, which is the opposite of what it anticipated.

WHERE THE UNIT FIXTURES DID COLLAPSE, and why that is not a contradiction:
three tests failed, every one of them built deliberately on adjacency — a
row of three disjoint bodies, a hue seam at `11200 -> 00112`, a bar and a
dot landing BESIDE an L. Those fixtures existed to exercise the dilation,
so they fell with it. The corpus does not lean on it nearly as hard.

AND THE COMPARISON EXPOSED A SCOPE THE LINE DOES NOT NAME. On one row,
`{} loops` is a PER-FORM quantity read off `form.loops.len()` while
`defects: …` is a CUMULATIVE process total read off a thread-local that no
form resets, so `0 loops … non-simple 3` reads as a form carrying three
defects and no loop to hold them.

THE FIX IS NOT TO MAKE THE COUNTERS AGREE ON SCOPE (corrected the same
day). A first reading of this called it two scopes on one line and asked
for one scope, and that is wrong about what a defect IS. An orbit count is a
property of a FORM. A defect is a CAUTERIZATION EVENT in a trajectory —
the moment a loop was terminated by being read — and the process-level
total is the honest carrier for it. The two scopes are correct and
different; what the line owes is to SAY WHICH IT IS PRINTING, not to
collapse one into the other.

### 60.6 The order of the work

1. PURGE the stencil in `pairing.rs` (`star_and_site_faces`). Incidence stencils go universally or the nerve
   keeps two topologies (58.3's own argument, one level up). Re-take
   `b_1`, `orbit_defects` and the spectra afterwards: they are expected to

2. THE TETHER, on `(N, D^2)`, off `Blade`'s centroid and `radius2`, with

   spellability.
3. THE KERNEL over the `Z_2` gauge freedoms of the half-open edges, which

4. THE MIND, once the third axis of an idea is ruled (59.10):
   `Contemplation::link_new` off `by_chart` key-sharing and off
