5. THE COURT's adjunction path on the demands the refused tethers emit,
   which is the first live work 37.7 has ever been offered.

## 61. Hue is a coordinate of the fibre (ruled 2026-09-22)

59.10 left the third axis of an idea unruled and T6 blocked on it. The
ruling closes a question `extract.rs` has carried open since the form's
chart was built.

### 61.1 The ruling

THE BASE MANIFOLD IS THE TWO-DIMENSIONAL SPATIAL CONTINUUM, projected onto
the raster as `(r, c)`. THE HUE IS THE FIBRE: a discrete field value — a
gauge state, a scalar charge — living over that base point.

`Link = (r, c, before, after)` is exactly a fibre morphism written out:
`(r, c)` is the fixed base point and `before -> after` is the transduction
occurring entirely within the fibre over it. The pair was never two
coordinates of one space; it is one coordinate and one state change.

### 61.2 What it settles, and what it obliges

IT CONFIRMS THE RENAME. `coord::Lamina`'s (since removed) third axis was named `hue` and
was fed `support_of`'s third component, which is the FRAME — the corpus's
own `e_3`, 51.3's sixth adjacency direction, the axis `at_frame_zero`
recentres. Under this ruling the colour could not have been there, because
colour is not a coordinate of the base at all. The rename was right and is
now ruled rather than inferred.

IT DECOUPLES THE MOMENTS FROM THE FIBRE. Where `blade::shape_of` demands a
third component to compute the harmonic multipoles, it is conflating a
fibre state with a spatial axis. The hue decides WHICH CELLS BELONG TO THE
BODY — it is the partition `pieces_of` splits on — but the moment tensor
is a purely spatial invariant of the footprint. The centroid `P`, the
deviatoric `u`, the quartic `h4` are properties of `(r, c)` and of nothing
else.

So `shape_of` must accept a purely spatial support. `before`/`after` stay
on the carried piece, where they dictate the METABOLIC TRANSMUTATION, and
they do not enter the kinematic shape tensor. That is what unblocks T6: a
remainder's links give `(r, c)` and need no invented `k`.

A.11'S SINGLE PRODUCER IS UNTOUCHED. The multipoles come off `blade::lift`
and nowhere else; this narrows what `lift` is given, never who computes it.

### 61.3 What it does not settle

The FRAME remains a third axis and is not the hue. `pieces_of` splits by
hue and then takes 6-adjacent components across `(r, c, k)`, which is
51.3's connectivity across frames, and `support_of` writes that `k`. The
ruling says the palette is fibre; it does not say the succession axis is a
spatial dimension to take moments over. Whether `lift` integrates over
`(r, c)` alone with the frame carried beside it, or over `(r, c, k)` with
the frame as a genuine third extent, is a separate question and is not
answered here.

## 62. Every component has two halves, and the pivots are the machinery (ruled 2026-09-22)

A physics component is a CONJUGATE PAIR. One half alone is a ratchet: it
accumulates and never returns, which is bookkeeping under a physics
name. The engine has named halves without the inverse halves in four places,
and all four are pivot machinery.

### 62.1 The ledger

```
  THE PIVOTS — three conjugate pairs, dimension-changing
    ascend    /  descend    seal a 1-cycle with a 2-cell / hollow it out   (2 <-> 1)
    condense  /  drain      form a tether from tension   / dissolve it     (1 <-> 0)
    puncture  /  seal       open a hole, injecting a class / cap and kill it

  THE METABOLIC PAIR — not a pivot; it changes no dimension
    dilate    /  contract   rho  <->  rho^-1
```

SIX PIVOTS IN THREE PAIRS, AND EXACTLY ONE IS BUILT. `ascend` is
`coboundary_on_link`; nothing else exists. A complex that can only GAIN
2-cells is the ratchet in its plainest form.

THE SIXTH PIVOT IS `seal`, AND IT WAS MISSING (named 2026-09-22). `puncture`
destroys a top-cell to open a hole, injecting a homology class; `seal`
glues a cap over that hole and kills the class. Standing alone, `puncture`
lets the engine TEAR A MANIFOLD AND NEVER HEAL IT, which is the ratchet
again on the other side of the complex. Naming `seal` closes the pivot set
under conjugation, and a first reading of this that called `puncture` a
self-inverse involution was wrong.

`dilate / contract` IS A CONJUGATE PAIR BUT IS NOT A PIVOT (reclassified
the same day). A pivot changes dimension; `rho <-> rho^-1` does not. Its
home is the METABOLIC layer of the functor, separated from the kinematic
translation `T(t)`: a scale change in the base is a boost along the null
direction `e_inf` in the conformal embedding, which is why `D(rho)` looked
conformal-rather-than-isometric where it sat. The pairing was always sound;
the organ was wrong (U7).

**Amended 2026-10-11 (ruled: the multi-axial pivot machinery is
ascend, descend, condense, drain and puncture, and `seal` is
authorized).** The six pivots in three pairs stand as ruled, `seal`
authorized as `puncture`'s conjugate, and they are the MIND's pivot
machinery: each mind runs them on its own complex, driven by its breath
(`dilate / contract`) and its three shells (MU-CLIENT §1, §4.3–§4.5). "Exactly one is built" no longer holds: all six are built on the Čech
complex (`src/transducer/cech/coboundary.rs` `ascend`, `descend`, `drain`;
`src/transducer/cech/hole.rs` `condense`, `puncture`, `seal`;
`src/transducer/cech/board.rs` `Pivot`, `Complex::apply`).
On the mind's own complex (`Contemplation.complex`): a held ring ascends
and punctures, and seals on collapse or on a discharge of its class
(`bubble/question.rs`, MU-CLIENT §4.5); a link's tether is written by
`set_edge` (the climb then ascends its cells); a retracted thought's star
drains and descends (`vent_vertex`). The construction's process-wide tally is
deleted: a pivot's outcome is returned to the field that applied it.

### 62.2 What this corrects

`condense / drain` IS TENSION AND RELAXATION, and 59's tether is those two
and not a new operator. A first statement of T2 read "a tether condenses
when `mu` is inside the horizon" and never said what releases it when the
strain leaves — half a component, and a 1-skeleton that can only grow.
The tether is `condense` given its physics and `drain` given its inverse,
and the two land together or neither does.

`dilate / contract` IS PIVOT MACHINERY, not a passenger. `D(rho)` has been
riding inside the carriage, and U7 recorded that as hygiene — "conformal,
not an `H^3` isometry, and it rides there anyway". It is not hygiene. It is
half of a pivot sitting in the wrong organ, and its conjugate has never
been named because the operator it belongs to was never recognised as one.

`puncture` IS NOT THE UNPAIRED ONE, and reading it as a self-inverse
involution was wrong. It is a pair like the others and its second half is
simply unbuilt and unnamed.

### 62.3 Why this decides how T2 is built

`REFUSE_EDGE` is a STATIC GATE and is correct as it stands: it re-derives
the transition on the two bodies' union and compares exactly, with no
threshold and no constant to dial. What it has never had is a physically
generated input — every edge it ever judged was minted where
`ring_of_support` inflated two disjoint supports until they collided.

The gate fires at the SETTLING, not at the coupling. Tension says two
bodies are coupled; relaxation says a coupled pair settles into the
transition it will hold, and that settled transition is what an
independent organ can re-derive. So a tether built as condensation alone
gives the court nothing to verify: a relation that can only appear has no
resting state to check against.

LAW 6'S TWO-ORGAN CONDITION HAS THEREFORE NEVER HELD HERE. One organ
generates the relation, another re-derives it; with the generator a
stencil and the relaxation absent, the court has been verifying the
internal consistency of an artifact. Both halves of `condense / drain` are
what make `REFUSE_EDGE` an organ rather than a formality.

### 62.4 Every loop is cauterized, and none runs indefinitely

A loop is not walked out of; it is TERMINATED BY BEING READ.
`rebase.rs` already says it for the stabilizer orbit — "the engine does not
step out of the orbit, it EVALUATES the orbit, and the orbit becomes a class
the form carries" — and the same holds for every cycle the complex stands.
`classify` is the cauterization: `Filled`, `Congruent`, `Class`,
`Unspellable` each convert a walk into content and stop it. An orbit with no
classifier is an orbit that runs forever.

THIS IS A THIRD KIND OF TERMINATION. Law 1 admits two — an integer measure,
or a `Budget` — and a cauterized orbit is neither. It ends because it was
READ, not because a counter was spent, and that is why a stroke can be cut
mid-cover without leaving a half-evaluated cycle: the reading is atomic
even where the walk is not.

So `orbit_defects` accumulating across a process is not an instrument
sloppiness. It is the ledger of cauterizations along a trajectory, and it
grows because the engine keeps exiting orbits and entering others. What it
must not do is print beside a per-form count without naming its scope.

### 62.5 A pivot changes dimension because re-entry is forbidden

No orbit is re-entered from the orbit just exited.
That is the condition that makes a pivot a pivot: having cauterized a
cycle, the walk cannot resume it, so the only move available is out of the
dimension it stood in. `ascend` takes a cauterized 1-cycle to a 2-cell;
the walk does not come back down into the cycle it just closed.

CONJUGATE IS NOT UNDO, and this is what saves 62.1's pairs from being a
ratchet running backwards. `descend ∘ ascend != 1`. Creation and
annihilation are conjugate without the second undoing the first in the
same step, and the same holds here: `descend` from a 2-cell reaches a
cycle, but never the one `ascend` closed to make it.

THE FAILURE TO COMMUTE IS WHERE THE CONTENT IS. If the two halves
commuted, ascend-then-descend would return the walk to its start and
nothing would have been gained — the pair would be a pure oscillation, as
empty as the ratchet is one-sided. `[ascend, descend]` is the curvature the
pivot carries, which is the same shape the algebra already has in
`[p, p] subset k` (Thomas precession, 60.4): two boosts do not commute,
and the boosts' commutator is a rotation that neither of them is.

So a conjugate pair is well-formed exactly when its two halves fail to
commute, and the commutator is what the pivot RETURNS. A pair that
round-trips is not a component; it is a no-op written twice.

**Amended 2026-09-23: `ascend` IS THE INVERSE OF
`descend`.** The paragraphs above conflated two things. ON CONTENT the
pair is an exact inverse: `descend` of the cell `ascend` sealed hands back
the fill that was sealed, exactly, and leaves the boundary 1-cells
standing, each with its transport unchanged; `ascend` of a released boundary
that still closes re-seals the same content. `[ascend, descend] = 0` in
the algebra, and a pair that does not invert on content is a ratchet with
a sign error, not curvature. What does NOT return is the TRAJECTORY and
the LEDGER: re-entry stays forbidden — the circuit resumes at a later `K`
on a new orbit, never the one it exited — and the ledger keeps the pair as
history, syntropy booked at `ascend`, and at `descend` the reading of
78.7: ELASTIC where the class is restored and the lane's draw returns,
VISCOUS where it is not and the difference is entropy. The content the
first draft put in the commutator lives there, on the class and the
ledger, and the Thomas-precession analogy was two boosts, not a pivot and
its inverse; it is withdrawn. Row AD1 tests the inverse on both poles.

## 63. T2 landed — the tether and its release (ruled 2026-09-22)

*Historical.* The record of the landing of 59's tether and of its conjugate
`drain` (62), the two halves of `condense / drain`. What still binds is
stated per section below.

### 63.1 The metric half: `Strain { num, den2 }`

The strain between two bodies is a ratio that is never evaluated: `mu` is
irrational, so the rational pair `(num, den2)` carries it and every question
is a comparison of cross products, split on sign before squaring (a negative
`num` is the common case). `num = 0` is orthogonality (`delta = 0`), not
tangency (`delta = 1`); the reading is scale-free (Axiom C); and on the
conformal sphere `num = -2 (s_a . s_b)`, so the strain is bilinear, an inner
product rather than a pairwise walk. The `Strain` carrier itself is
superseded by SQ1: the tether `V = s_b s_a` is carried whole
(`src/transducer/blade/tether.rs`, `tether`), and `(num, den2)` is only a
reading of `V`'s class where a side or a regime is asked (`Contact::of`).

### 63.2 The conjugate half: `drain`

`drain` is a dimension-1 cauterization, the event `classify` performs on a
cycle one dimension down (62.4). An edge in the boundary of a coface that
has been read is pinned and cannot drain; the cofaces are read as the keyed
meet `star(a) ∩ star(b)`, never as a walk of the higher degrees. Strain
cannot vanish: `g_ab = 1` returns the 1-cell to the vacuum, `g_ab ≠ 1` is
classified and the reading travels out, and nothing is written to a coface.
`forget` is the exact inverse of `remember` over the degree layer, the degree
index and each vertex's star, so no ghost incidence is left. The hue cycle of
a 1-cell is `Identity`: a 1-simplex is contractible and carries only the
connection.

### 63.3 The ratchet moved up a dimension, and then stopped

A pivot whose conjugate is missing moves the ratchet up a dimension: while
`descend` did not exist, `drain` returned `Pinned` naming a remedy nothing
could perform, and a 1-cell inside a 2-cell was immortal. `descend` is
`drain` one degree up, deliberately: the same dimensional gate, the same
pinning from above by a keyed meet (`star(a) ∩ star(b) ∩ star(c)` against
the 3-skeleton), the same `forget`, and the same refusal to write into a
neighbour. A 2-cell that sealed no circulation descends `Unsealed`, with no
class invented. A 2-cell carrying a fill no longer hands its class out
alone: as ruled 2026-10-20 it descends as `Descended::Throat`, its class kept
as a hole. The ladder, every row built (62.1 as amended):

```
    dim 2   ascend  ────────►   seal a 1-cycle with a 2-cell
            descend ◄────────   re-open it, unpin its boundary
    dim 1   condense ───────►   mint a tether from strain
            drain   ◄────────   release it, cauterizing
    dim 0   puncture ───────►   open a hole, inject a class
            seal    ◄────────   cap it, kill the class
```

### 63.4 Binding

```
src/transducer/blade/tether.rs       tether, Contact: the strain carried as V = s_b s_a (SQ1)
src/transducer/cech/coboundary.rs    drain and descend, forget as remember's inverse
src/transducer/cech/hole.rs          condense, puncture, seal
src/transducer/cech/simplex.rs       Drained — Vacuum, Cauterized, Pinned, Absent
                                     Descended — Unsealed, Throat, Pinned, Absent, Hole
src/transducer/cech/tests/drain.rs   drain's outcomes, the pinning rule, the cycle with no ghost
src/physics/axioms/tests/tether.rs   the regime read exactly and scale-free; num and den2 as a second derivation
```

## 64. The envelope: why the luminal ray sits outside the harmonic core (ruled 2026-09-22)

The strain's invariance under a common motor is PROJECTIVE and not exact,
and that is not a defect in the derivation — it is the classification. A
ray is not a rigid motion on an interior manifold; it is the outer
conformal hull that wraps the harmonic bodies and mediates between them.

### 64.1 The hierarchy

```
    LUMINAL ENVELOPE        [M] in P Spin+(4,1)(Q)      the ray
        weight              lambda = M M~               gauge scale
        invariants          degree 4: den2, I_2         the screw
        carries             refraction, transvection
              |
              |   refraction across the interface
              v
    HARMONIC CORE           s^2 = +r^2 > 0              spacelike
        moments             m in {2, 3, 4}
        provides            den2 > 0                    no null collapse
```

The compact stabilizer `Spin(3)` literally SITS INSIDE `Spin+(4,1)`, whose
ten generators are three rotations, three transvections, one dilation and
three special conformal accelerations. The luminal group contains the
harmonic one; that containment is the envelope, not a metaphor for it.

### 64.2 Why the core must be strong, and why it already is

`s^2 = +r^2`, so `r^2 -> 0` drops the nucleus onto the light cone,
`den2 = 4 r_a^2 r_b^2 -> 0`, and the inversive distance diverges: the
interaction horizon stops being DEFINED, not merely large. The harmonic
moments are the mass that resists conformal collapse.

The smallest body the sensor can deliver is ONE LAMINA, and it reads `r^2 >=
1/6 > 0` — because `blade::lift` integrates the lamina's own unit square
and carries the parallel-axis term at every order. A POINT-MASS READING
WOULD GIVE `r^2 = 0` AND COLLAPSE IT ONTO THE CONE; a second, point-mass
trace of the same quantity is a law-12 defect — two producers of one
quantity — and is retired. It is not cosmetic: A.11's single producer is
what holds every nucleus spacelike.

### 64.3 Refraction is the dimensional drop

```
    g_ab = (theta_b theta_a^-1) . gamma_ab
```

The ray does not pass through the harmonic boundary unchanged. It BREAKS:
`theta_b theta_a^-1` is the projection into the nuclei's planar orientation
frames, where the sensor sees `l in {1,2,4}` or a parity flip at `m = 3`;
`gamma_ab` is the residue that REFUSES TO FLATTEN, and it is where `I_2 !=
0` lives when the relative motor carries transverse displacement or
isoclinic tilt (60.4).

### 64.4 The weights do not cancel; they are QUOTIENTED

A first statement of this said the projective weights "cancel out" around a
closed circuit. They do not. Each edge carries its own `lambda_i`, and the
orbit product `Omega = g_ca g_bc g_ab` accumulates `lambda_a lambda_b
lambda_c` as ONE overall scale. What removes it is the COMPARISON:
`same_versor` is `projective_ratio(a,b).is_some()`, an exact rational ratio
over `Q^x`, so the reading is taken on the ray and the scale is quotiented
at the point of asking.

THE DIFFERENCE IS OPERATIONAL. "The gauge disappears" would license
comparing `Omega` to the identity with `==`; "the gauge is quotiented"
says that comparison is WRONG and must go through `same_versor`. The
engine already does this, and it is exactly where a bug would hide.

### 64.5 What may be keyed on

NEVER THE BARE NUMERATOR. `num -> lambda^2 num` and `den2 -> lambda^4
den2`, so keying on either keys on the gauge shadow. Only the ratio is
invariant, and it is invariant ON THE NOSE:

```
    delta^2 = num^2 / den2      unchanged under a common motor, measured
```

That is a SINGLE exact rational, reduced canonically by `BigRational`, so
it is already a scale-free coordinate with no normalisation step and no
root. A pair's address is that value together with the side, and the side
is read by `Strain::side` (since removed) rather than off `num`'s sign (63.1).

AND THE SIDE SURVIVES A NEGATIVE-NORM MOTOR — measured, not argued. This
stood open on the question of whether `lambda = M M~` can be negative.
`Cl(4,1)` is INDEFINITE, so it can: `e_1 e_-` has `M M~ = e_1 e_- e_- e_1 =
e_1 (-1) e_1 = -1`, which a definite signature never produces. The sandwich
`M x M~` is `lambda` times an orthogonal map, so the inner product picks up
`lambda^2` — and `lambda^2 > 0` for EVERY `lambda` in `Q^x`, negative ones
included.

So `Strain::side` is an ABSOLUTE geometric invariant: the sign it splits on
cannot invert through an indefinite reflection channel, while `num` itself
remains gauge. The pair `(side, delta^2)` is therefore fully characterised —
scale-free, root-free, reduced canonically, and stable under every motor
the algebra admits.

## 65. Five regimes, and attention as a vector (ruled 2026-09-22)

Two scalar collapses, found by asking where `condense` should be antipodal
and why `STROKE` is still a constant. Neither was in the metric; both were
in what the metric was read INTO.

### 65.1 The inversive spectrum has five regimes, not three

```
  Contained   TangentInt     Intersecting    TangentExt    Apart
   d < -1       d = -1        |d| < 1         d = 1        d > 1
  ---------]------|------[-------o-------]------|------[---------
                               d = 0
                            (orthogonal)
```

`Contact` had three arms — `Through`, `Tangent`, `Apart` — reading
`Tangent` only at `delta = 1` and folding the whole lower half into
`Through`. So `delta = -1`, INTERNAL TANGENCY, where two spheres touch at
one point from inside at `d = |r_a - r_b|`, was reported as
interpenetration. Both `delta = +-1` are genuine codimension-1 contact
interfaces, and calling one contact and the other penetration lost the
boundary's symmetry. That is a scalar collapse committed in an enum rather
than in a metric, and it mislabelled half the contact locus.

THE FIXTURE HID IT. A body against ITSELF sits at `delta = -1`, where
"touching from inside" and "fully overlapping" are both defensible — so the
assertion passed while testing what was written rather than what is true.
The case that is not ambiguous is two DIFFERENT bodies at `d = |r_a - r_b|`,
and the corrected test exhibits it.

READ EXACTLY AND WITHOUT A ROOT. `|delta| = 1` is `num^2 = den2` with the
sign of `num` choosing which tangency; the rest is `delta` against `+-1`
through `delta_at_most`, which splits on sign before squaring.

### 65.2 The antipodal involution

`sigma: s -> -s` is the same sphere with INSIDE AND OUTSIDE EXCHANGED. It
sends `delta -> -delta`, so it swaps `Apart` with `Contained` and the two
tangencies with one another, and FIXES `Intersecting`, whose own fixed point
is `delta = 0` — inversive orthogonality, `d^2 = r_a^2 + r_b^2`.
`sigma . sigma = id`, and no regime outside the secant band is fixed.

WHAT SURVIVES IT DECIDES WHERE A GATE MAY READ. `delta^2 = num^2/den2` is
antipodally invariant; the SIDE is not, because the involution flips
`num`'s sign. So an orientation-blind gate reads `delta^2` and receives the
dual pair `{Apart, Contained}` and `{TangentExt, TangentInt}` as single
orbits; a gate that requires an exterior interface rather than containment
reads the arm. `Blade::nucleus` is the single producer of a nucleus's
orientation (law 12), so the sign is canonical in practice — but that is an
invariant of ONE FUNCTION and not of the algebra, and it is stated here
rather than assumed at every call site.

### 65.3 Where `condense` belongs: the two poles, not the pullback

```
    FAMILY POLE (matter)            BUBBLE POLE (morphism)
    entities  bodies                entities  carriages
    generator nuclei s in Q^{4,1}   generator motors M in P Spin+(4,1)
    condenses spatial bonds         condenses kinematic entanglement
         |                                 |
         +------------ PULLBACK ------------+
                 cover_deformation
                  (chart overlap)
```

WIRING `condense` INTO `cover_deformation` WOULD BE A CATEGORY ERROR. The
cover's meet index is built on PULLBACK INCIDENCE across carriages, which
are morphisms `domain -> codomain`; the field is between BODIES. Running it
there inherits the carriage ontology and lets a body tether to its own
replicate — which may be wanted, but as a ruling and never as a default.

So the field runs at each pole on that pole's own entities, and
`cover_deformation` keeps its integrity as an atlas pullback: it answers
chart overlap, which is a different relation and remains true.

### 65.4 `STROKE` is a scalar standing where a vector belongs

`Budget` counts calls to `spend()` — IMPLEMENTATION EVENTS, not physical
work. That is why the cover test's `STROKE = 4` decayed silently when the
ring stencil went: the same deformation cost fewer `spend()` calls and the
constant stopped forcing the resume it was written to prove. A constant
denominated in an implementation detail tracks the implementation, and
every refactor falsifies it without touching the physics.

AND IT COLLAPSES THE FOUR LANES LAW 5 READS SEPARATELY. Attention is
ALREADY a vector here — `Bubble.escrow` is "the mu-vector drawn from the
voice's reserve to keep it, per lane", and "a mind rich on `h` and spent on
`S` holds turns and withholds placements". A single integer expresses
neither half of that:

```
    A = (S, G, T, H) = (scale, gauge/rotor, translation, hue/fibre)
```

A mind at `[0, 10, 10, 5]` has exhausted DILATION and retains turning and
sliding. Under a scalar stroke an expensive dilation attempt burns the
global counter and preempts it out of the lanes it could still afford,
which is unphysical.

`Reserve` DRAWS A VECTOR, ALL OR NOTHING, AND REFUSES PER LANE. `Depleted`
names which lane could not cover the draw, what was asked and what was
held — because "the mind is out of attention" and "the mind cannot afford
THIS, on the scale lane" are different facts and only the second says what
may still be attempted (rule 11). An action with a ZERO PROJECTION on a
depleted lane remains affordable, which is the whole content of the
anisotropy. And `restore` is its conjugate: an escrow that can only be
spent is the ratchet of 62 one level down.

### 65.5 The observer is the boundary condition

```
    metric      mu_c    <->  the alphabet's spellable reach     (59.6)
    temporal    STROKE  <->  the reserve's anisotropic lanes    (65.4)
```

Neither belongs in the engine as a constant. `mu_c` is how far a mind's
alphabet reaches across the conformal quadric; the stroke is how many
topological phase changes its four-lane escrow can afford before it yields.
Both are properties of the OBSERVER rather than of the substrate, and both
were numbers standing where a derived quantity belongs.

WHAT IS BUILT AND WHAT IS NOT. `Reserve`, `Depleted` and the vector draw
are built and proven. `Budget` still counts reads and still bounds the
cover; the two are not yet joined, and the stroke will not be physical
until a draw replaces the tick at the call sites and `cursor::park` lands
on a CAUTERIZATION rather than at an arbitrary count (62.4). That join is
PHY1, ruled in 78.66.

## 66. The field fired, and the refusals named themselves (ruled 2026-09-22)

*Historical.* The first census of the field at the family pole. It found
contact refused by gates placed in the wrong operator and split each fused
refusal into named arms: `relative_rotor` returns a typed refusal (now
`NoPose`, `src/transducer/blade/frame.rs`) rather than one `None`, which is
rule 11 at the producer, and the metric refusal keeps `Apart` and
`Contained` apart (65.2). Its figures were taken against one-hue bodies and
do not survive chapter 70 (70.5). Three rules still bind: a congruence test
belongs to the quotient operator and never to contact (a square may touch a
rectangle); the operators divide by inversive regime, so no single gate
swallows both poles of the antipodal involution (contact itself is now read
topologically, A.14, 69.3); and an unspellable relation is emitted for the
court to adjoin a letter against two vantages (37.7), never discarded with a
`continue` and never carved into the base stack by hand. The axioms A.12 and
A.13, raised here, govern.

**A.12 — irreducible inversive extent.** Every body is spacelike, with
`r² = Tr(I)/M₀ ≥ 1/6 > 0`: one lamina's floor is `n/12`, the unit
`n`-cube's second moment summed over its axes, and `1/6` is its value at
`n = 2` on the sensor plane (64.2, 72). The moment tower is normalised by
`M₀`, so harmonic order `m` carries degree `m`:

```
    ‖M̃_b^(m)‖² · (r_a²)^m  =  ‖M̃_a^(m)‖² · (r_b²)^m
```

Register: `src/physics/axioms/native.rs` (`A12_IRREDUCIBLE_INVERSIVE_EXTENT`).

**A.13 — inversive momentum and the conformal conjugate pair.** Translation
and special conformal transformation are one generator seen from opposite
poles, exchanged by inversion `I`:

```
    T_i = e_i ∧ e_∞   fixes ∞          K_i = e_i ∧ e_o   fixes the origin
    K_i = I · T_i · I⁻¹
```

so that a body can arrive from infinity; a motion built of translators alone
fixes the point at infinity. Momentum is the inertia paired with the
carriage between sections, `Π = I · g_{k→k+1}`, the `S` lane against the `T`
lane between frames, never a derivative (law 1). The momentum half is built,
`Π = M₂(B)` (78.52 Row 1; `src/physics/tensegrity.rs`, `momentum`,
`external_torque`); the inversive half `K_i` stays docketed (REG1;
`src/physics/axioms/native.rs`, `A13_INVERSIVE_MOMENTUM_DOCKETED`).

### 66.3 What the corpus actually says

*Superseded by 67.1 and 68.2.* It read every `Oblique` refusal as an
unspellable turn, 37.7's condition. That overstated it: a pure reflection
also reads `Oblique`, so the arm straddles the permanence axis (67.1) and is
split into `Mirrored`, `Incongruent` and `Oblique` (68.2).

## 67. A refusal is a perspective, and only a mutable one is a demand (ruled 2026-09-22)

66 reported "75 of 118 contacts are oblique" as though it were a property of
the corpus. It is not. It is a property of THIS READER, whose epigenome has
adjoined nothing. 60.1 already said it — what a mind cannot spell, it cannot
connect — and the census is the reading of a mind that has learned nothing.
Five voices, five censuses, on one scene.

### 67.1 The axis that cuts across the five arms

`NoPose` sorts refusals by MECHANISM — where the reader gave up. The
operative distinction is PERMANENCE — whether any alphabet could ever change
the answer:

```
    IMMUTABLE  Bodiless, Isotropy, Unoriented, reflection
               facts about the geometry; no vocabulary alters them.
               A final reading.

    MUTABLE    an unspellable turn
               a fact about the READER's vocabulary, which grows.
               A demand.
```

ONLY A MUTABLE REFUSAL IS A DEMAND. A demand minted from a reflection does
not merely ask for a generator that is not a turn — it asks the court to
change something that cannot change by learning, and minting one would
corrupt the group: no adjunction takes `O(2)\SO(2)` into `Spin+(4,1)`.

`Oblique` STRADDLES THE AXIS, which is exactly why it cannot be emitted
wholesale, and why 66.3 overstated it.

### 67.2 A refusal must never be stored; the relation must be

Writing `NoPose::Oblique` onto a cell would FREEZE A PERSPECTIVE — the
verdict of a mind at one moment, preserved past the vocabulary that produced
it, with nothing to re-read it when the next adjunction makes it false.

P9 already rules the shape and it had not been connected: `Bubble.candidates`
is "populated at hold time by RE-DERIVATION from the demand's own bodies and
never stored beside them (law 12)". The demand carries the GEOMETRY, not the
conclusion, so every hold re-reads against the CURRENT alphabet and a mind
that has learned since gets a different answer from the same held thought.
That is the superposition pulled back into the mind — not re-sent,
RE-DERIVED.

So the emission is not "emit `Oblique`". It is "emit the relation" — the
bodies and the bodies' measured relative bivector — and let the verdict be a
function of who reads and when. `Demand::RotorPrime`'s witness is shaped for
it: it carries the BLOCK THE PRIME WAS READ OFF, never the conclusion.

A per-pass tally is safe on this count: taken and cleared per pass, a
reading of one traversal and not a stored verdict. But it is why THE CENSUS MUST BE
RE-TAKEN AFTER EVERY ADJUNCTION rather than treated as a measurement of the
corpus.

### 67.3 Two vantages are what turn a perspective into a fact

One voice reporting "this cannot be spelled" is a perspective and has no standing.
Two organs independently RE-DERIVING the same generator — `witness_rederived`
-> `converge_witness` -> `home_install` — is how it becomes structural. That
is law 6, and it is why the emission belongs to the distributed layer: the
base stack can only ever report its own perspective and has no standing to
promote one.

### 67.4 Precognition is the gate on the return valve

Moved to [MU-CLIENT.md](MU-CLIENT.md); see its Rulings index.

### 67.5 Binding

```
transducer/blade/frame.rs               NoPose's arms — sorted by mechanism,
                                        and the permanence axis cuts across them
transducer/bubble/idea.rs               candidates re-derived at hold, never stored
server/cognition/germinate/listing.rs   open_unspellable, docket_letter — the promotion
```

## 68. The instruments, and what they measured (ruled 2026-09-22)

*Historical.* The instruments asked for on every bivector plane, on
entropy, syntropy and metabolic rate, and on every gate, and the readings
that showed three of four first placed at sites that could not answer. Its
figures were taken against one-hue bodies and do not survive chapter 70
(70.5). The rule that binds: no counter without its denominator and no
reading without an askability bit, so a zero says WHERE flow stopped, and an
instrument sits where the quantity is produced, never on a cold site or a
type with no production callers.

### 68.1 D1 — the plane census, and two wrong placements

Ten counters, one per bivector plane of `Cl(4,1)` (generated from `n`,
71.2(3)), split into the harmonic six and the luminal four, so a reading
gives DIMENSIONAL CAPACITY rather than throughput. One producer takes both
halves of a transition `D(ρ)·T(t)·R`, the carriage and the rotor, so a
transition is counted once and a screw can be seen; and the census is taken
where the rotor has been EXTRACTED, since a composite versor's raw grade-2
part lights `eᵢ∧e₋` from a pure translation. Equal counts on `eᵢ∧e₊` and
`eᵢ∧e₋` are the translator's signature — `T = 1 − ½t∧e_∞` puts equal weight
on both null poles — and are ONE fact, not a boost. Code:
`src/transducer/cga/planes.rs`.

### 68.2 V1 — the oblique split, recut in `Cl(4,1)`

`Oblique` answered for facts of opposite permanence, so it is split:
`Mirrored` (improper), `Incongruent` (the bodies differ in a quantity no
conformal motion changes), and `Oblique` (NOT PROVED PERMANENT). Chirality
is read by an ODD invariant of the body's own normalised tower,
`Z = h₂² · conj(h₄)`, rotation-invariant and conjugated by every reflection
whatever its axis — never by a table of `D₄`'s improper elements applied to
cell coordinates, which is a Euclidean flattening. Chirality answers the
odd question only: A.12's scale certificate is the even half, and both
gates must pass.

### 68.3 The odd harmonic, and the quartic branch's missing turns

The tower carries the odd harmonic `h₃ = Σ(x+iy)³/M₀`, exact on laminae
with NO correction term (a unit square's own odd moments cancel, so the
point-mass formula IS the integral). Two consecutive orders give the
relative turn outright — `z₃·conj(z₂)` has argument `3φ − 2φ = φ` — exactly,
over ℚ, at any relative scale. `h₃ = 0` exactly when the body has 2-fold
symmetry, so `HalfOpen` is a property of the BODY rather than a gap in the
reader. A moment of azimuthal order `m` turns at `m·φ`, so the quartic
branch admits EVERY 90° turn.

### 68.4 D3 — the mint, and the four gates that can refuse it

A refused relation is carried into a demand, never dropped by a bare `?`.
A rotor is a RAY, a Gaussian integer `w` with `arg(w) = φ/2` and `w⁴ ∝ z`
up to a POSITIVE rational, so the spellable set is exactly `z ~ +1` and
`z ~ −1`. Four gates, every one able to refuse the mint: `Oblique` and
nothing else; ORDER 2 only (the court cannot tell which harmonic produced a
block); a PRIMITIVE arc (a composite mints letters the court can only throw
out); and a prime the alphabet lacks (`z ~ ±i` names none).

### 68.5 D2 — the ledger, and what μ is not

Entropy is a cauterization (`Drained::Cauterized`), counted apart by the
skeleton it terminates; syntropy is READ from the producer that already
counts a condensation, never duplicated; the orbit is `ℓ = Order(R)`, the
discrete structure `μ` is CARRIED BY; the rate is the reserve's draw and
restore per lane, four lanes never summed. `μ` is the engine's kinematic
charge, related to the inversive distance by `μ = (δ−1)/2`; carrying a
second quantity under that name (field energy as `μ = δ²`) is declined, the
defect A.12 was raised to fix in the harmonic tower. Code:
`src/physics/metabolism.rs`.

## 69. The censuses, and the ground they stood on (ruled 2026-09-22)

*Historical.* The withhold, horizon and contact-family censuses, taken
against one-hue bodies; chapter 70 supersedes that ground and 70.5 rules
that none of the earlier numbers survives unchanged. The withhold census made the
classification of a withheld form a structure (`Withheld`,
`src/transducer/family/deflation.rs`) and caught a vacuity: a tree has
`H¹ = 0` by construction, so its cochain is a coboundary trivially, and
`Acyclic` is its own arm, never folded into `CoboundaryResidue`;
`is_mutable()` stays false for it, because on a tree the answer is unknown
rather than yes. A.14, stated in 69.3, governs.

### 69.2 The horizon turns away bodies that are touching

The strain band `1 < δ ≤ 2` admits only equal-sized bodies in contact: a
single cell edge-to-edge against a bar of length `n` reads `δ² = 4` at
`n = 1` and is turned away as `Apart` for every longer bar. `δ = 2` is the
inversive distance of two unit cells at distance 1, not a similarity class
of adjacency; the scale-free proof holds when both bodies dilate together,
never under independent scaling. So the band cannot decide WHETHER two
bodies touch; that is topological (69.3, A.14).

### 69.3 A.14 — the moment tower cannot carry contact

A sound pair reading is CONSTANT on a contact family, and neither the
rank-1 reading `Tr(I)/M₀` nor the rank-2 directional reading is: both grow
along a cell against bars of growing length. A second moment is an RMS
SPREAD and contact is a BOUNDARY, so no finite-order tower of the two bodies
taken SEPARATELY recovers a boundary; and a multipole contraction fails
because a unit cell's deviatoric VANISHES, so `tr(Ĩ_A Ĩ_B)` is identically
zero on the whole family. (The rank-2 record, a Euclidean quadratic form, is
retired; `Contact::of` reads the sign of the weight `V Ṽ`, never `s · s`
against `B B`.)

**A.14 — a body-pair relation is the same primitive that defines a body.**
A body is a connected component under lamina incidence; two bodies are in
contact iff an incidence edge joins them. The incidence is read off the
ordering (`src/transducer/sentence/chain.rs`, `face_incidence` and
`contact_cells`), never a distance test against every lamina, and the
invariance obligation is met BY CONSTRUCTION because the reading never
consults extent.

NOT ONLY A COUNT. The contact face is the SET of edges with the edges'
coordinates and its edge transport (50.3) — a tally IN PLACE of the set would
discard the interface it was meant to name. The edge count beside the set is a
lawful reading (Concordance 1.10).

The `δ` machinery is not wrong and is not removed: `Strain`, the five
inversive regimes and the antipodal involution soundly say WHAT a relation
is like. They were being asked WHETHER one exists, which is topological and
was answered upstream.

## 70. Hue is a fibre, not a base — chapter 20 superseded (ruled 2026-09-22)

**Amended 2026-10-09 (U13; recorded verbatim in §0.1).** This
chapter governs what a body is at intake, and U13 rules on its two
pre-decisions: hardcoded colour heuristics are abolished, and the void and
merging are MEASURED by the Mayer–Vietoris sequence, never assumed —
assuming them "imposes an affine, coordinate-level bias on a cohomological
space. It pre-empts the physics."
- *Merging is the connecting map.* 70.4's ruling "a body is a maximal
  HUE-BLIND connected region of the support" — every face adjacency joins,
  so touching colours merge into one body — is SUPERSEDED as a
  pre-decision. Two touching bodies U and V are one body U∪V iff the
  transport holonomy around the bodies' shared contact face U∩V is the identity
  (Ω = id); where it is non-trivial they are two interacting bodies
  separated by curvature. The probe evaluates the cycle holonomy to decide
  the boundary. 70.4's hue-blind region stays a reading of the cover, and
  its gauge seams (`δ⁰θ = θ_bθ_a⁻¹` within a body) are exactly the
  transports whose holonomy the measurement reads; the one-hue split 70
  retired stays retired — U13 restores neither pre-decision.
- *The void is the boundary channel.* Hue 0 read as void (`if h != 0`,
  78.158 (c)) is SUPERSEDED: colour 0 is the e_∅ gauge reservoir, the
  point at infinity and sink; a body does not vanish into it, its
  constructors pass into the e_∅ boundary condition, tracked as a
  measurable flux and never deleted (law 7; ∇B of U15, 78.68 as amended;
  78.58's reservoir — the identification of channel 0 with 78.58's
  ancilla is §0.1's open (ii)).
- *The route.* Both are scene-cover readings and law 6's clause governs
  them: offered to the court by probe and ruled with a receipt, never a
  code change on one side (53.2's roster). The former U12 of 78.158 —
  `scene::cover`'s bands and `peel_body` reaching the residue's complex —
  is folded into this route: those readers are what the Mayer–Vietoris
  measurement is taken over.
- 70.6 and 70.7 (the contact as shared boundary and as a chart) stand:
  the contact face U∩V they build is the face whose holonomy decides.

Chapter 20 ruled on 2026-09-09 that A BODY IS ONE HUE. Two weeks of
readings say it cannot stand: it makes perception MONOCHROME. A body
defined by its colour is not a body seen in colour — it is a body seen
one colour at a time, which is the absence of chromatic reception rather
than an implementation of it.

### 70.1 What the one-hue rule actually built

`components()` reads the scene's whole 6-incidence and keeps one half:

```rust
    let edges = incidence_of_3d(&positions)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|&(i, j)| sorted[i].3 == sorted[j].3)   // ← same hue only
        .collect();
```

Over 40 tasks and 128 scenes:

```
    732 hue-blind regions  →  1646 bodies      2.25 bodies per visual region
    single-cell bodies     1053 of 1646        64.0%
    contact pairs touching a single-cell body   816 of 1102   74.0%
```

AND ONE NUMBER FIXES THE STRUCTURE EXACTLY. The contact graph's component
count is 732 — the same as the hue-blind region count. That is not a
coincidence: what 69 measured as a "contact graph" is precisely the
INTERNAL GAUGE STRUCTURE of 732 visual objects. Its edges are colour
seams inside objects; its components ARE the objects.

Which corrects 69's own reading. `b₁ = 188` is NOT inter-object cycle
structure. Those are orbits WITHIN multi-coloured objects — a ring of one
colour about a centre of another. They were reported as the manifold
gaining cycles; they were never between objects at all.

The decomposition:

```
    598 monochrome objects  →  1 body each, no seams        the "isolated" 36.3%
    134 polychrome objects  →  1048 bodies, 7.8 fragments each,
                               carrying all 188 loops
```

### 70.2 The defect has a name: fibre data in the base

Everything downstream of perception ALREADY treats hue as a gauge the body
carries — `Carriage.sigma: Vec<(u8,u8)>` is the hue map, `𝒢` is the gauge
lane, `CycleType::of(gauge)` reads its cycle type, `hue_pair_key`
coordinates it. Perception alone treats hue as the body's IDENTITY.

That is fibre data placed in the base, and monochrome vision is what it
produces. A body is WHERE MASS IS; its colour is what it CARRIES.

### 70.3 Hue is a luminal ray, and that is why it is a fibre

The ruled framing, and it is the one that makes the split
dimensional rather than merely tidy: a hue is a RAY, presented in the
luminal layer as a fibre at a higher order, and DEPTH is the distance
between rays. Harmonic perception and luminal/ocular perception are then
separable layers a single mind can hold at once.

D1's census is the evidence that the luminal layer has never been
inhabited. Over 368 transitions:

```
    e1p 20  e1m 20        e2p 25  e2m 25
```

`eᵢ∧e₊` and `eᵢ∧e₋` carry IDENTICAL counts, which is the translator's
signature — `T = 1 − ½t∧e_∞` puts equal weight on both null poles. Those
four counters are ONE fact and the engine never boosts. The luminal half
is populated only by translation's shadow.

An engine with no chromatic perception has nothing to put in its ocular
layer, and the census says exactly that.

### 70.4 The ruling, and why its two halves cannot land apart

**A body is a maximal HUE-BLIND connected region of the support. Its hue
is the gauge section it carries, not its identity.** *(The first sentence
SUPERSEDED 2026-10-09 by U13 as a pre-decision: touching bodies merge
only where the holonomy around the bodies' contact face is the identity — see
this chapter's amendment. The second stands.)*

1. Bodies become the 732 visual regions, not 1646 shards. The colour
   seams stop being discarded filter noise and become the body's own
   gauge section, `δ⁰θ = θ_bθ_a⁻¹` WITHIN a body. That is content, and it
   is precisely the cocycle that stays ASKABLE when a form's 1-skeleton is
   a tree — 69 measured `delta1()` vacuous on 34 of 36 forms and had
   nothing else to read.

2. Inter-body contact needs its OWN primitive, and this is the half that
   must land with the first. **Every site of the shape (ruled
   2026-09-22):** `pieces_of` takes the cover's pieces hue-blind, never
   filing a body's laminae by hue first, and 13.9's "a seam between two
   hues is a meet" is superseded here — the seam is the body's gauge
   section and never a meet between pieces. Under hue-blind bodies two distinct bodies
   can never be 4-adjacent — if they were, they would be ONE body. So
   cross-hue incidence stops being the inter-body relation and becomes
   intra-body gauge content, and A.14's contact primitive is left with
   nothing to range over. DIAGONAL incidence is the replacement: exact,
   integer, in the face incidence's own idiom, no bounding sphere and no
   band.

LANDING (1) ALONE COLLAPSES THE ENGINE into 732 isolated islands with no
external pathway at all — a worse famine than the one 69 diagnosed, and
arrived at deliberately. The halves are one ruling.

**The contact graph.** Bodies are hue-blind components of the face
incidence, one for each hue-blind region. A contact lies between two
distinct bodies, never inside one: the incidences between two hues within
a body are its gauge seams, content and not contact. Contact is read as
the cells of lower grade two bodies share (`contact_cells`; the shared
boundary, 70.6), and its cycles are the first cycles between bodies, where
70.1's were all inside objects. `named_faces`
(`src/transducer/family/pairing.rs`) offers a face for each contact,
tagged `Contact`; a pair that several incidences name is one face carrying
all of them.

### 70.5 What must be re-measured, because every 69 reading moves

`b₁ = 188` is internal and must be re-read as gauge content. The
famine census, the withhold census, the plane census and the metabolic
ledger were all taken against 1646 shards and will read differently
against 732 bodies. No number from 68 or 69 survives this unchanged, and
none of them should be quoted forward without a re-run.

The demand-kind census found 189 demands over the corpus forms, none of
them `RotorPrime` or `Standing`, the two kinds `list_demands`
(`src/server/cognition/germinate/listing.rs`) could open; the rest were
source, creation and topological-deformation demands, which it skipped. The
growth organ of 37.7 was never offered an item of a kind it can open; the
zero of 45.9 is a consequence of that and not a finding about the court.

Taking the cover's pieces hue-blind removed every orbit, chord and cover
meet the corpus carried: each came from a boundary between two hues inside
one body, which under 70.4 is the body's gauge seam, read as gauge content
and never as a meet. Restoring the per-hue split to keep those counts is
refused: fibre data does not go back into the base to keep a count up.

A contact is one face per body pair (C1), and the frame axis adds the pairs
that touch across frames: a family is read as its frames stacked along
`e₃`, and a body pair may touch across a frame boundary and nowhere else,
which no corner in one frame can see.

THE WALK ORIENTS BY MEMBER PAIR (O1). A walk that decides which way it
crosses a face by the face's two vertex ends reads the pair key backwards
on a face whose two ends are one vertex. So the walk and the forest cross a
face by the member pair it holds: forward where it holds `(c_from, c_to)`
with `from` at its `i` end, and backward where it holds the pair the other
way round. A face holding both, on two charts, refuses as `two ways` rather
than taking one; the unread arms are `CircuitUnread`
(`src/transducer/cech/orbit_algebra.rs`). Read so, the first inter-body
cycles are flat. Where a cycle's edge half is refused as `not rigid`, it is
because 50.3's edge was written for two bodies one versor carries, and two
bodies meeting at an edge or a corner are carried by two. That is C3–C5's
question, the transport through the interface's own frame (70.7), and O1
does not answer it.

```
transducer/blade/body.rs         components() — every adjacency joins; hue never decides identity
transducer/sentence/chain.rs     face_incidence — the 1-skeleton; contact_cells — the contact
transducer/family/perceive.rs    perceive_at — where laminae become bodies
transducer/element/gauge.rs      hue_pair_key, the gauge coordinate hue belongs in
```

# Part XIII — The physics as the only producer, and the rulings (chapters 71–80)

## 71. The base is ℚⁿ and n is data (ruled 2026-09-23)

The ruling: there are no static dimensions. The number of base coordinates is a
coordinate of the corpus, discovered at intake and carried as data, never
a type, a tuple, a constant or a list of directions; the planes of the
algebra are generated from it; and what is true of ℤ³ is a row of a
family, missing context in ℤⁿ. A crystal with a fixed dimension is flat
in exactly the way the last two weeks were spent leaving: a chart whose
axes were declared rather than read.

### 71.1 What Phase C hardcoded, and what each is in general

| hardcoded in Phase C | the fact it is a row of |
|---|---|
| `DIRECTIONS`, ten named directions in `chain.rs`; twenty adjacencies plus six faces | the neighbourhood `{−1, 0, 1}ⁿ ∖ 0`, `3ⁿ − 1` neighbours, generated |
| "edge" and "corner", "in-frame" and "across-frame" | the GRADE of the cell two cubes share: `m` coordinates differ, the shared cell has dimension `n − m`; `m = 1` makes a body, every `m ≥ 2` is a contact of grade `n − m`, and the set of differing axes is a coordinate of the contact |
| `(i64, i64, i64)` for a site, a direction, an interface element | a point of ℤⁿ, its length carried with it |
| `put_face` writing three `i64` per element | the address writing `n` first (the coarsest stratum, A21) and then the coordinates |
| `[Q; 32]`, `BLADES = 32`, ten planes | `Cl(n+1, 1)`: `n` point generators with `e₊, e₋`, `2^{n+2}` blades, `C(n+1, 2) + (n+1)` planes, the harmonic and luminal split generated from the signature |
| moments on three axes | A.11's tower on `n` axes (38.2), carried as ratios of homogeneous forms (Axiom C) |
| tests asserting 20, 6, 16 | tests asserting the grade relation and the generated count at the corpus's own `n` |

### 71.2 The ruling

1. **`n` is read at intake.** The corpus presents its base coordinates —
   two grid axes and the frame axis today, `n = 3` — and the intake writes
   `n` into every carrier that holds a site. Nothing downstream names an
   axis by position; a reader asks the point its length and the set of
   axes on which two points differ. Chapter 51.2's choice of `Cl(4,1)` over
   `Cl(5,1)` stands as the VALUE at `n = 3` and is superseded as a method:
   the algebra is `Cl(n+1, 1)` and its blade count follows `n`.
2. **Contact is by grade, never by name.** Two bodies relate where the bodies'
   cube complexes share a cell of dimension `n − m`, `m ≥ 2`, read off the
   occupancy in canonical order as today; the grade and the differing
   axes are the contact's coordinates. "Across the frame axis" is the
   reading `e₃ ∈ differing axes`, a fibre of that coordinate, not a
   census column of its own.
3. **The lift is into `Cl(n+1, 1)` and the planes are generated.** A site
   lifts to the null vector `X(p)` exactly over ℚ; a support's conformal
   content is the blade its null points span where they span one (a point
   pair, a circle, a sphere — grade at most `n + 2`) and its tower
   otherwise; the harmonic planes `eᵢ∧eⱼ`, `eᵢ∧e₊` and the luminal
   `eᵢ∧e₋`, `e₊∧e₋` are enumerated from the generators at `n`, never
   listed. D1's plane census reads a carrier of `C(n+1,2)+(n+1)` counters.
   The letters are unchanged (law 6): the seventeen act on the planes of
   the sensor chart they were written on, and a plane a larger `n` opens
   receives a letter by 37.7 or not at all — which is what "planes come
   and go" means here, and why adjunction and not a table is the organ
   that answers a new dimension.
4. **The crystal is generic and still not content.** The geometric product
   over exact ℚ for a signature `(p, q)` is one interpreter with the
   signature as its parameter; two courts replaying one another agree on
   the signature because it is on the address (`n` first). Nothing in this
   makes the interpreter content (1.8, 1.9).
5. **Refused on sight from here:** a tuple of coordinates as a type above
   the sensor boundary; a constant naming a blade count, a plane count or
   a neighbour count; a list of directions; a census column named for an
   axis; a test that asserts `20`, `26`, `32` or `10` as a property of
   the geometry rather than of the corpus's `n`.

6. **Topology at any `n` is exact homology by ranks, and the chart is a
   locator** (ruled 2026-09-23, with the implementor's four corrections).
   The complex is named: a support's cube complex is the CLOSED UNION of
   its unit cubes on ℤⁿ, a finite complex whose boundary maps have
   coefficients in `{0, ±1}`; its Betti numbers are `βₖ = dim Cₖ −
   rank ∂ₖ − rank ∂ₖ₊₁`, the ranks exact over ℤ by fraction-free
   elimination in `core::lattice`, refusing on overflow — the one place a
   matrix is allowed, because it holds an integer rank and nothing else
   (A18). That retires `β₁ = β₀ + β₂ − χ`, a formula true on a 3-complex
   only, and the mixed complex it read. A boundary map has as many
   columns as the complex has cells, so beside `z_rank<const N>` a
   sparse, variable-width exact rank is written once (row BQ4). Under
   ranks the chart's `β₀` is the union's `H₀`: two parts touching only
   at an edge or a corner count as one, and the `n = 3` charts move
   wherever that happens, mainly on the fibre unions — the census reads
   the move before and after, named with the number. BODIES STAY DEFINED
   BY FACE ADJACENCY (70.4, 71.2(2)); the chart's topology is the
   union's. Cost is measured, never assumed: the census wall time
   before and after is the instrument, and free-face collapse is the
   known reduction if it is needed. STRATA OF DIFFERENT `n` ARE
   DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION: the address writes `n` first, so a chart at
   `n = 3` is never a prefix of one at `n = 4`, and the count axes are
   generated from `n` (`β₀ … β_{n−1}`, then the rest) without being
   prefix-stable across `n`; within one `n` A21's prefix rule holds as
   before. A claim that the `n = 3` block is a prefix of the `n = 4`
   block is refused. AND THE CHART IS A LOCATOR: the physics decides
   congruence and contact — the tower, the frame, the tether — and the
   chart only finds the candidates a reader then measures (53.1, 59.4);
   Betti numbers are acceptable in the chart only under that sentence,
   which is the answer to the flat-shadow concern.

### 71.3 What this costs, and the order

It touches the crystal's carrier (`Mv`), the lamina, the site codecs and
every plane-indexed instrument, so it lands as its own phase, doctrine
first, and Phase O's C4 and C5 are cut UNDER it: an interface lifted into
`Cl(n+1, 1)` with `n` on its address, not into a fixed `Cl(4,1)` with a
site list. O1, the orientation fix, is independent of `n` and lands
first. 70.7's rulings — the interface as a chart, the contact as the
2-simplex, identity by address — stand and are re-read at `n`.

```
core / transducer/cga        Mv over Cl(n+1,1): blades 2^(n+2), the
                             signature a parameter, the product generic
transducer/blade             Lamina = (Vec<i64> of length n, hue); lift on
                             n axes; the tower to the order 38.2 rules
sentence/chain.rs            neighbourhood generated from {−1,0,1}ⁿ;
                             contact by grade and differing axes
sentence/chart.rs            the address writes n, then coordinates
transducer/cga (D1)          the plane census generated from n
server/registry, arc.rs      n read at intake and written into the family
```

## 72. The physics is the only producer (ruled 2026-09-23)

The ruling, on the implementor's remediation list after
reading `src/physics` whole: **topology may decide whether two bodies
touch; the physics — the strain field, the frame reader and the
metabolism — is the only producer of what a contact is, what its
transport is, and what it costs.** A carrier built beside the physics for
a quantity the physics already produces is law 12's defect and is refused
at review (checklist (p)). Every row from here states which physics
quantities it reads and which it produces, and names the census it
expects to move, measured before and after.

### 72.1 The register, amended

- **A.10, restated — and the first statement retracted (ruled
  2026-09-23).** A first restatement squared the pencil,
  `(s_a ∧ s_b)² = (num² − den2)/4`, and read the interface off the sign of
  that scalar. That is law 11 in the form the law names: a square looked
  for inside a circle, a remainder (`√(r_a²r_b²)`) that never closes over
  ℚ, and the pencil of two spheres collapsed to a number. It is
  retracted. The manifold way is to act, never evaluate. Each nucleus
  has `s² = r² ≠ 0`, so it is an invertible vector, which is a versor:
  the inversion in that sphere. Two nuclei are related by the conformal
  motion the two inversions compose, **`V = s_b s_a`**, carried whole
  and applied by the sandwich `V X Ṽ` to whatever crosses the interface —
  a body, a transport, a cycle. `V` is the tether of 59 and 62, exactly the whole product
  `Interface::between` computes before it splits it by grade; the split
  into a strain and a blade was the flattening, and `V` is held instead.
  `V`'s kind is read the way every versor's is, by its class invariants
  and the defect classification the orbit reader already runs (trivial,
  elliptic, hyperbolic, parabolic, non-simple): around intersecting
  spheres it turns about the spheres' common circle, at tangency it is
  parabolic, between separated spheres it is a boost or a dilation. So:
  two bodies co-occupy through the conformal motion the bodies' inversions
  compose, carried as a versor and applied, never squared into a scalar;
  the luminal case is `V` parabolic, read from what `V` does. Curvature
  is where a cycle of such motions fails to return, read as holonomy —
  the triangle `V_AI · V_IB · V_BA` of the contact 2-simplex (70.7).
- **Axiom C, tightened.** A relation is carried as the versor that
  performs it, and applied; a ratio of homogeneous forms of equal degree
  is read only where a classification is asked of a versor — its class,

  `δ² = num²/den2` and `μ = ⟨Ω⟩₀²/⟨ΩΩ̃⟩₀ − 1` are the same projective
  reading of `V`, Study's condition on a ray, and they stay as readings
  of `V`'s class where one is asked; every site that carries or gates on
  such a square instead of on `V` is censused and ruled site by site (row
  SQ1), since some are the projective comparison Axiom C permits and some

- **A.11, extended.** The tower carries the odd harmonic `m = 3` (68.3),
  and is stated on `n` axes as the traceless symmetric moments of each

- **A.12, derived from `n`.** One lamina's floor is `n/12`, the unit
  `n`-cube's second moment summed over its axes; `1/6` is its value at

- **A.13, promoted from docket to row** (A13): `K_i = I·T_i·I⁻¹` built,

Refused: the contact band `1 < δ ≤ 2` as a gate — a dialled `μ_c`

### 72.1b Each relation is carried at the grade of its simplex (ruled 2026-09-23)

The ruled correction of two flattenings in one derivation, and the
rule that follows. "Pencil" is struck: it is the two-body name for the
family two spheres span and not one of this document's nouns. The nouns
are **tether** — the horizontal relation between two bodies, `V_ab =
s_b s_a`, minted by `condense` and released by `drain` (59, 62) — and
**fibre** — what rides vertically over one body, its hue gauge and its
sections (61); a tether joins two fibres and is not one.

**The derivation that flattened.** `V_ca V_bc V_ab = (s_a s_c)(s_c s_b)
(s_b s_a) = r_a² r_b² r_c²`, "so `n` spheres alone carry no curvature",
made two mistakes that are one. It let the spheres relate only in pairs —
a triangle of pairwise tethers is a cycle in a graph, and a graph is
two-dimensional thinking, every relation between two things — and going
around the triangle it revisited each sphere, so `s_c s_c` appeared and a
sphere times itself is its square, `r_c²`. The flatness was PRODUCED by
that squaring (law 11), not found in the geometry: a body revisited is a
body squared, and a pairwise orbit always telescopes to a scalar. The
sentence is withdrawn.

**The rule.** An `n`-body relation is one object of the grade its
simplex has, each body taken once and never revisited. Three bodies
relate through the odd versor `s_a s_b s_c`, the composite of three
inversions, whose grade-3 part `s_a ∧ s_b ∧ s_c` is the three-way content
— the meet the three share — that no product of pairwise tethers can
carry, and whose order is its orientation. `n` bodies relate through
`s₁ s₂ … s_n`, reaching grade `n`; the content of `n` bodies lives in
grades 3 through `n`, and every one of those parts vanishes if the
relation is walked around in pairs. So each of the nerve's cells carries its own
grade: a 0-cell a body's nucleus, a 1-cell the tether `s_b s_a`, a
`k`-cell the `(k+1)`-fold product of its bodies. `ascend` seals a 2-cell
with its three-body versor, never with a check that three edges compose
to the identity; the coboundary (10.3, 10.4) compares a cell's own
versor with its faces', which is the non-abelian Čech coboundary with
the cell's content in place of a scalar. A `k`-cell exists where its
`k+1` bodies mutually meet — pairwise sharing boundary cells (71.2), or
through an interface chart (70.7) — which is the nerve's own simplex
condition (14.6).

**Curvature, re-read.** It is not only holonomy around 1-cycles. It
includes what the higher-grade parts carry that no boundary of pairs
reproduces; the 1-skeleton orbits read so far are the flattened shadow of
that. Around a 1-cycle the tether alone telescopes, and the holonomy
that survives is the frame against the inversion — `g_ab =
(θ_bθ_a⁻¹)·(s_b s_a)`, where `θ` and `s` do not commute — which is 60.4
met from the other side: the harmonic core and the luminal tether are
both required, and neither alone bends anything. O1's fifteen trivial
classes are those edges carrying no `θ`. A cycle's holonomy has two
parts, a geometric part (`θ` against `s`) and a gauge part (the fibre
permutation around the orbit), read together and never summed (law 5).

**Consequences for the rows.** BQ5a composes the frame with the tether,
or every contact cycle reads flat, and it is not enough alone: where
three or more bodies meet, the 2-cell carries its three-body versor as
content (NB1), the fibres riding every cell. BQ5b's face holds `V`
whole, as written. The nerve's certified triples (58.1, read 0 on 252
forms) are the 2-cells NB1 mints wherever three bodies mutually meet.

### 72.1c A frame is a section over a stratum of the base, never a still (ruled 2026-09-23)

The ruled reading: a step of `k` in `T` gives one "frame", and a
body already in motion is then frozen at that instant in two dimensions,
where the topology asked for should be examined instead. The freeze was
in the frame reader: `blade::Frame` and `relative_rotor` read a body's
orientation from planar harmonics of `x + iy` alone, so `θ` could only
ever be a turn in `e₁₂`; nothing was read across `e₃`; the planes
containing the succession axis stayed dark; and 52.5 already found and fixed this
once for the EDGE — a quotient at one frame has no `e₃` extent and its
loops read flat — while the frame reader never received the same fix. A
moving world measured through its stills.

**The word.** "Frame" keeps 1.4's sense: the sensor's plane in its
conformal model, with a carriage — the place a form acts. A slice of the
base at one `k` is a **section at `k`** (51.4), and a body's orientation
with its placement is its **pose** (vocabulary). `blade::Frame`, the
relative-orientation reading, is the relative pose and is renamed with
its row.

**The ruling.**

1. **A body is its tube, not its slice.** Along `e₃` a family is one body
   on `(r, c, k)` (51.3, 51.4). Its pose is read on the whole tube: `θ`
   is a versor over every plane the tube occupies — the planes containing
   `e₃` and the boost planes among them — read from the tower on `n` axes
   (BQ4, A.11 on `n` axes), never a planar turn.
2. **The motion is part of the body's state.** A.13 names it: momentum
   is the inertia paired with the carriage between sections, `Π =
   I · g_{k→k+1}`, the `S` lane against the `T` lane between frames.
   `Quotient { frame, car, … }` already carries that transition and has
   never been read as a momentum; A13 builds it, so a body carries its
   pose and its motion together.
3. **The span is a stratum of `e₃`, and it is content before it is a
   reading** (amended 2026-09-23 on the implementor's three questions,
   FR2: a stratum here is a keyed FIBRE of `e₃` coordinates, a set of
   sections, not a contiguous prefix; a cycle's span is the INTERSECTION
   of its vertices' sections, the sections on which every transport it
   composes exists, since a transport between two members exists only
   where both stand (51.4) — the union of what its vertices touch is the
   cycle's reach, a different reading; the span is DERIVED from
   `Form.sections` at the read and never stored beside it (law 12); and a
   demand names a stratum through its bodies' own sections, so `Demand`
   gains no field — where a reading proves a demand needs a span its
   bodies do not carry, that is an address change and a ruling's). The answer to "intrinsic or observer-relative" is both,
   split the way the document already splits content from reading. The
   span a relation closes over is CONTENT read from the form: a cycle's
   span is the sections its holonomy is read over, an orbit's is its
   period `ℓ`, a contact's is the sections its interface spans; it is a
   prefix of the base's `e₃` coordinate, a stratum (A21), read as a
   keyed fibre and never by walking `k` by `k`. What a mind or a court
   ASKS about is a reading of that content at a stratum — a demand may
   name a stratum (53.3), the horizon is spellability per mind (59.6) —
   and a reading never changes the content (law 12): where a cell's own
   span exceeds the stratum asked, the reading holds (rule 15) or refuses
   by name, and never truncates the tube to the still that was asked
   for. A fixed span, one `k` or any other constant, is refused (rule 5).
4. **The relative pose of two moving bodies is the transport between
   the bodies' tubes** over the span, in one exact lift, composed with the
   tether and with the `n`-body versor as before. The inter-section
   carriage then supplies what the frozen `θ` could not: the second
   Casimir from a turn against a displacement along `e₃`, which is
   exactly what makes a screw (60.4, the harmonic axiom test).

### 72.1d Motion is paced by the mind's universe, and memory hardens fibres into tethers (ruled 2026-09-23)

**The universe of a mind is the hardware it runs on.** Everything in
72.1c is the mind of the client, and its motion is relative to the
resources the mind has, never to a clock and never to another mind's
pace: a mind allocated a laptop and a mind allocated a farm read the same
mathematics from the same receipts (13.7) at different periods, and
neither races nor fights for resources, because the metabolic reserve is
calibrated once from the hardware present (`reserve_max`, the module's
own header: the scale is the machine's) and every motion is a draw on
that reserve per lane (65.4, PH4). Continuous motion is therefore
`k`-steps that are ORBITS — circuits of the mind's own carriers (45.7),
of the spheres whose congruence it is reading — and never frames per
second; the one wall-time value in the tree is the scheduler's parking
floor and no reading is taken from it (law 9). A stroke that draws
nothing moves nothing; a stroke that cannot afford a lane says which lane
and works in the others (`Depleted`).

**The plexus of memory, in the document's nouns.** Congruence forms in
the crystals: sections that agree on a stratum (23.9, 45.9). The
connection of fibres is then measured through torsion — what will not
close, filed at its period (A17, 25.5) — and where the orbits close the
form is coherent (2.2, 10.3). Coherence hardens by consilience: two
courts replay the closure (37.7, law 6). At that hardening a FIBRE
becomes a TETHER. The fibre is vertical and held — a body's gauge, its
sections, its held orbits, in the contemplation and the dialect, the
epigenome, short-term memory (25 as ruled 2026-09-19) — and the tether is
horizontal and ruled — the relation between two bodies, `V` with its
frame, a 1-cell of the genome, long-term memory on disk. The callus is
the transition from Stood to Ruled read at the relation rather than at
the word: a fibre the mind held becomes a tether the language carries
when the closure it took part in has been replayed twice, which is 37.7
at depth 4, a relator. Nothing is calloused by time, by count or by a
commit; only by replayed closure, and a fibre whose closure no court
replays lapses with its escrow (Z4d) and is never promoted.

**Binding.** `physics/calibration.rs` (the reserve as the universe), `physics/
budget.rs` (the draw), `bubble/` (the fibres held), `server/cognition/
book/` (the tether ruled), `client/sdk/epigenome/` (the callus, Stood →
Ruled at the relation).

### 72.1e Three clocks, and where the pose lives (ruled 2026-09-23)

**Three things that are not one.** The implementor's mapping of 72.1d
onto the tree holds, and one sentence in it is refused: "`k` is the
mind's own orbit index." Three coordinates are being named there and
they are kept apart by law 9 and chapter 51: `e₃`, the succession axis of
the BASE, is the corpus's own coordinate — the position of a section in
the family, content, never a clock (51.1); the mind's **orbit** is its
local time, circuits of its own carriers beside its `K` (45.7, `Orbit`);
and **TUniversal** is the mesh's height, read from receipts (45.2). The
`T` lane of μ⃗ stays what law 9 says: temporal extent counted in
receipts, a cost, never a coordinate. So a proposal that the `T` lane
advance per cauterized orbit, or that a section at `k` become a stratum
of an orbit ledger, is refused: orbits PACE how much of `e₃` a mind reads
per stroke (72.1d), they do not become its coordinate. What the proposal
rightly wants — a parked read resuming at a cauterization rather than a
count — is PH4.

**Metabolic relativity (A.18).** Content never depends on hardware; only
rate does. A.9 applied to time: two minds at two reserve sizes reach the
same forms in the same order, the larger reaching more of them per
wall-second, and a test runs one family at two reserve sizes and asserts
identical forms and orbits in content.

**The callus (A.19).** A relation is a fibre until its torsion is
discharged into coherence (`torse_relief`, the physics of the
transition) and re-derived on two vantages (law 6); then it is a tether,
and the court's install is the callus. A tether that drains deposits its
record or returns to vacuum, never silently (A.8). The fixture runs
fibre → torse → second vantage → tether, then drain → deposit (MEM1).

**Where the pose lives.** The pose of 72.1c is the BODY's: its
orientation with its placement, read on its tube, carried by its word
vertex (rotor and carriage) in the dialect while Stood and in the genome
once Ruled. It is neither the fibre nor the tether. The fibre rides over
the body (its gauge, its sections); the tether between two bodies
carries the RELATIVE pose `θ_bθ_a⁻¹` composed with `V`. So the tube
reading sits on the body from the moment it is perceived, the relative
pose enters the tether when the tether is minted, and both harden with
what carries them: the word by ratification, the tether by the callus.

### 72.1f The layer register, and four constraints on the callus (ruled 2026-09-23)

**The direction.** The mesh is the library of court-ruled, crystallized
knowledge; each client is a lean local mind holding only what its work
touches, at its own hardware's pace. A local installation is its own
epigenome plus the strata of the genome its tasks reach, fetched by
prefix (A21) and never searched; the syllabus teaches only ruled words
(`serve_ruled_never_teaches_provisional_word`).

**The layers may hold different axioms, and the boundary is shared.**
Mind and mesh can specialize above one core, or no court could re-derive
a client's word (law 6). The register:

| layer | axioms | where |
|---|---|---|
| core, shared | the interpreter — the geometric product over exact ℚ and the canonical forms (1.8, 1.9); the address layout with `n` written first (71); the two-vantage rule (law 6, 47.3); law 11; A.8 | every binary |
| mind only | metabolic relativity (A.18); volatility of the epigenome (25); spellability per mind (59.6, 60.1) | the client |
| mesh only | consilience (37.7, 67.3); persistence (28, the genome on disk); deposition (A.8, a drained tether leaves its record) | the courts |

Specialized nodes are strata of the library: a hypha serving one region
of knowledge is a keyed fibre by chart or class, an A21 prefix — which
the cover trie already is (MU-ENGINEERING §4, `nerve::home` by chart
prefix). Row SN1 parks it until the language exists to be served.

**Four constraints on the callus (MEM1), each a correction of a text
relayed 2026-09-23.**

1. No "zero internal strain" and nothing "dissolves without trace" (A.8).
   Torsion is promoted, annihilated against a partner, or deposited; a
   tether carries whatever its holonomy is; a drained tether leaves its
   deposited record. Forgetting without trace is the ratchet run
   backwards.
2. No `∮dθ` and no "relaxed into its minimal geodesic" (law 1, 59.8).
   The reading is the holonomy: the ordered product of the tether
   versors around the cycle, cauterized by being read. Relaxation is
   local; there is no globally minimized action.
3. A tether is not a generator. Most hardened relations are spelled in
   letters the alphabet holds; only a relation proved unspellable adjoins
   a letter, through 37.7, or the alphabet inflates against the
   minimality the syntropic stroke prunes toward (E2).
4. `δ⁰θ = θ_bθ_a⁻¹` is the gauge cocycle, not the torsion. Torsion is
   what the cocycle fails to close to around a cycle, exists only on
   cycles, and under 72.1b is read at the grade of the simplex, never
   edge by edge.
