### 78.16 The deployment checklist, and the typed instruments

Four checks bind a deployment. (C1) A build ships from committed code only. (C2) All nodes are upgraded at once, never rolling: the wire's decoders refuse an unknown reading tag whole, and courts of different versions can disagree on one certificate's replay. (C3) Nothing prints per stroke (PL1 at every site): the percept holds its typed readings and prints no line, a test prints its own lines from those readings, and a running node's readings are read on the observer only, with no mode flag. (C4) Tape compatibility is verified read-only against a form an earlier build wrote. The instruments are typed and served on demand, never a clock (law 9): the reads each reader spent per stroke and the `Unbounded` refusals by reader (BD1), the progress readings off what is already produced (contact cycles with non-trivial holonomy, certified cells by grade with round kept, closure class and dual frame, refusals by grade), and an observer query by source and by reading kind through the prefix key, so large readings are not cut by the reply's frame budget. Code: `src/server/cognition/court/phase.rs`, `src/observe/store.rs`.

### 78.17 A court's phase is a typed reading

Historical in its readings (the first measurement after the Stage 22 deployment: adjoined-by-closure zero on every mind, no contact cycle yet read with non-trivial holonomy). Two rules stand. VS1b: a held orbit's classes are read once before the bend trials, a pair whose orbit has no class is counted `no-class` without a read spent, and the trials stay last in the percept, so a spent stroke leaves the instrument unread and never perception; no share of the stroke is set for an instrument, since a share is a dial. PH5: a court's phase is a typed reading, `Reading::Phase`, served on the observer beside the learning curves and never a printed line. Code: `src/observe/reading.rs` (`Reading::Phase`), `src/observe/fleet.rs` (`Phase`).

### 78.18 BQ5a: the contact edge is refraction

A half-open pose carries every candidate (two for a held `ℤ₂`), the contact edge across it forms a COSET of refractions, and a piece at one frame forms a static edge `Static(V)`; a circuit through a coset reads closed, closed modulo the held `ℤ₂ᵏ`, or open with no representative, and the union-rigidity path is out of the contact edge at every site. Every refusal carries its kind through one reader of what the refusing reader carried (CV1).

- (a) A mixed contact (one member transited, one at one frame) forms a static edge and keeps each end's pose as far as it was read, the missing one named, so a later arm can complete the refraction; a half-known refraction is not fully unread (rule 11).
- (b) PG1 counts a coset circuit apart from the curved ones, by its closure: a held superposition is not a class.
- (c) The static tether `V = s_b s_a` is read from the two bodies the face names (BD2's body pair, the pair's nuclei), never from a member's union support.
- (d) CT1's other-circuits arm compares every kept circuit sharing a face (R3, T1 on two routes between the face's ends), by a keyed read of the face's fibre, never a pair walk.
- The candidates multiply per held step (`2^k` for `k` held `ℤ₂` steps): the enumeration spends the stroke's budget per candidate formed and refuses by name when spent; the exact reader for large `k` is T5's kernel.

Code: `src/transducer/sentence/transport.rs` (`Static`, `HeldPose`), `src/transducer/sentence/pivot/refracted.rs`, `src/transducer/sentence/compose.rs` (`CosetUnbounded`), `src/transducer/family/pairing.rs`.

### 78.19 CT2: the constructed route

Where every reuse arm is empty, a lost step is completed by a CONSTRUCTED route: the tether `V = s_y s_x` of the lost face's two bodies' nuclei, from the witness cells holding both, carried by each other constructor the cells hold, `s_k V s_k⁻¹`; T1 is read on the two routes between the lost face's bodies (the constructed one against the rest of the circuit, available only where every other step reads, by name), giving flat, or curved with its holonomy. A circuit only a constructed route reads is a CANDIDATE: its offers (arm, face, constructor ray, verdict, holonomy ray, modes) are volatile on the circuit reading and never installed, and the offers' broadcast is CV4's. This cell-level construction is R3's; the member-level construction, a member carried by a constructor the mind's dialect holds to a new chart pair, is row CT2b, where the dialect's constructors are those offered across the mesh. Code: `src/transducer/family/pairing.rs`, `src/transducer/sentence/pivot/refracted.rs`.

### 78.20 The vocabulary sweep: circuit and trajectory, never walk or descent

The engine's motion is named the circuit, the read, the traversal or the crossing, never a walk, and a reading with no measured motion is "no trajectory", never "no descent" (VT1, VT2): the circuit reader lives in `src/transducer/sentence/pivot/circuit.rs`, and the withheld kind is `Withheld::NoTrajectory` (`src/transducer/family/deflation.rs`). Kept by sense: sheaf descent, Fermat's descent, the pivot pair `ascend`/`descend`, the receipt chain's ancestry traversal, and the iteration of a plain carrier, a carrier read not being the engine's motion; the keyed trie's `walks` module keeps its name (`src/network/nerve/keyed/walks.rs`, A13's own for the carrier's reads).

### 78.21 The TUniversal clock is core functionality

The engine's time is TUniversal and each node's own `K`, never a wall clock (law 9); a TUniversal clock is built into the servers as core functionality, so that any reader orients on the universe's clocks and the disparity between them without a wall clock. On 72.1e's three clocks:

1. **Three clocks, named apart on every reading.** TUniversal is the mesh's height, the receipt chain's head as this node admitted it, `1 + max(h(prev), parent heights)` (47.2): the one clock every node shares and the only one comparable across nodes. A court's `K` is its own count and a voice's `K` its own (72.1d); two `K`s on two nodes are two clocks, and the clocks' ratio is not a disparity of time. Disparity is read in height only: per peer, the last height this node admitted from it and the gap to its own head; across nodes, the spread `max − min` of heads. A gap in height is a reading of replication (13.7, CV5), never a fault and never a threshold (rule 5).
2. **`Reading::Clock` per court**, typed and served: its `K`, its head height, the genesis it started from, per peer the last admitted height and the gap, and the heights at which its ledger, registry and eras were last persisted, so that "how long since persisted" is a difference of heights and of `K`, never of seconds.
3. **A per-voice clock**: its `K`, its court's height when last heard, its genome's last-persist height.
4. **The console header places every source on TUniversal first**, by height with its own `K` and the spread, before any other reading; no wall-clock value appears on the console or in any reading. As corrected by 78.152: what remains is the one scheduler floor, `physics::stroke_floor`, the bound of a park on no work, told to the OS scheduler and read by no one; every bound on work is counted in strokes or in final-point advances.
5. **Every reading is quoted against height and `K`.**

**A tick is a frame (amendment).** `S, G, T, H` are the four dimensions of one tick: each TUniversal tick is a FRAME of the `{S, G, T, H}` manifold, so the ledger has four dimensions, not solely a height; height is the tick count along the causal order of 45.3, and the same tick's extent reads on `T` as a duration in receipts, on `S` as a scale, on `G` as a gauge count and on `H` as a fibre span (65.4).

- (i) The stamp is six fields, `h : S : G : T : H : k`: the tick, the frame's four lane extents, and the `k`-step of the node that stamped it; with 78.23's place it prints `h:S:G:T:H:K.i` (row CK1). C6's refusal of `XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX` stands only for a bare height dressed as a clock.
- (ii) Each combination of `S, G, T, H` at a tick is a manifold tied to a `k`-step, held for reconstruction in superposition (the hold and vortex of 25 and 59.5): a thought's escrow per lane at the height it is paid to.
- (iii) 73.19's refusal of the event coordinate is retracted (the frame is adopted, `H` included); its refusal of a probability stands (law 1).
- (iv) `Reading::Clock` carries per source the stamp and per tick window the frame, and the console prints every source by its stamp.
- (v) Disparity is read on the tick and per lane: two nodes at one height whose frames differ hold different manifolds of the same moment, and that difference is content, never a fault (13.7, rule 5).

Code: `src/observe/clock.rs` (`CourtClock`, `Clock`), `src/chronometry/receipt.rs` (`KStepReceipt::print`, `CoreStamp`), `src/server/cognition/reads.rs` (`core_stamp`), `src/bin/mycelium-server/console.rs`, `src/physics/calibration.rs` (`stroke_floor`).

### 78.22 Framing refusals, and a citation is coordinates, never a copy (LD0, LD1)

- **The head advances on parents only.** Only a parent admission advances a head (47.2); back-fill never does, and a proposal that it should is refused. A node that hears a cover digest cites its signer's head as a parent on its next receipt (45.2).
- **LD0, refusal at the writer.** A writer that cannot frame what it was given refuses the whole write by name and writes no partial frame; a discarded refusal (`let _ =` on a framing call) is the defect at every site, and a silent truncation such as a count cut at `u16::MAX` refuses by name. The underlying shape is R6's: an index copies the address.
- **LD0 as re-ruled: no widening.** Widening a length prefix treats the symptom; the `u16` stays as the wall and refuses loudly, and a write that reaches it is a blob written where a coordinate or a citation belongs, fixed at that site. Three kinds of bytes are never confused. A COORDINATE is written inline by its type's own `put_canonical` in A21's order (a rational by its exact length, a versor as its canonical ray, an invariant and a chart each by its coordinates), never as a nested key. An ADDRESS, a form's M2 composite (17.2), is held once, where the form is held (K6). A CITATION locates a held form by exact coordinates and never ships its bytes: the fibre (the class record and the chart; a form's fibre is its chart alone, 78.24(2a)) with the admitting act's stamp as the exact locator; the form's whole M2 travels once, in the act that admits it; across courts the citation carries the court's `vk`; where identity must be verified without the chain, the form's vertex charts (53.6) are its own coordinates.
- **Rows and deltas.** An escrowed award is a field of its word's row wherever the word is held (provisional, listing, cavity or basis), moving with install and written once with the row; a receipt delta cites by the locator; raw composites (a cocycle row's gauge, dialect transitions, closures, the verdict-attach `g`, the pivot certificate, the syllabus rotor) are each persisted as its canonical ray, or as the class record where only the class is read.
- **Dead writers are deleted, not repaired** (TR1). The verdict act is deleted whole and its code byte left unassigned: a court's ruling reaches a node as a receipt through the exchange and its back-fill (45.2, 47.2), and two courts reach one verdict with no exchange of opinion (13.7, 23).
- **LD1.** `Reading::Carriage` measures, per carrier and kind, the records, bytes and largest: awards as the treasury persists them, receipt deltas by act kind, wire frames by act tag; the proof of LD0 is a carriage flat in the form's size and bounded by `n` and the rationals' precision.
- **C4 widened.** The tape check reads every carrier the build under check wrote (genomes, ledgers, registries, eras), not the genomes alone.
- **Persistence.** The receipt chain is the record; the ledger, registry and eras are derived from it (law 12), and a restart replays the chain from a snapshot's height to the head.
- **EC1.** A ruling's release, demotion or slash is applied by the node that admits its Ruling receipt (78.24(b)).

Code: `src/transducer/address.rs` (`put_address`), `src/chronometry/receipt.rs` (`Cite`), `src/observe/carriage.rs` (`Carriage`), `src/economy/persist.rs`, `src/economy/escrow.rs`.

### 78.23 A k-step is one orbit of a planet around its star

1. **The `k`-step is one orbit.** A planet's (a mind's) `K` counts the completed orbits of its own carriers around its star, one circuit under its reserve (72.1d), and the completion of an orbit fires the stroke (perceive, think, express, learn) on everything the orbit crossed. *(Withdrawn by §0.0: `K` is a ledger coordinate (OK1), never an orbit.)*
2. **One orbit, one tick.** The receipts an orbit's acts admit stamp one frame `{S, G, T, H}` at one TUniversal tick (78.21); every client runs its own orbits under the same tick, and the frame's coordinates make each orbit unique at that tick (78.21(v)).
3. **Distance from the star is a planet's own, and equal frames are a collision.** A planet's radius is its orbital element (74: the stratum depth of its charts, read on the clock as LC1's dialect span); two planets whose frames coincide at a tick are a COLLISION (74's perspective collision), and separation is a transport under measured pressure (76.3, CR1), never a slot, a table or a timer.
4. **The register (OK1).** `K` advances by one where a cycle closes by name, the court's cycle (exchange, deliberation, lapse, persist) and the voice's cycle (quote, utter, learn, syntropy) each sealing the orbit boundary, and by nothing else.

**The orbit on the stamp (ACT1-orbit).** The stamp is `h : vk : K : i`, coarsest first: the tick, the signer, the orbit and the act's place `i` within it, reset at each close. Every act stays a node at its own stamp with its Parent reference and `admitted_at`; folding an orbit's acts into one receipt is refused. The height stays per act, `1 + max(h(prev), parents)` (45.2, HT1), and the orbit's tick is the `h` of its closing act. Each act keeps the frame it measured; the orbit's frame is read as the per-lane sum over its acts (law 5) and reported at the closing act's tick, derived and never carried (law 12).

**No orbit collides.** Each kernel's orbit is the fibre over its key in its star's field (73.15), distinct by construction, with no assignment, slot or table. A collision is prevented, never named after the fact: at the orbit boundary, before the closing act is stamped, the orbit's frame is compared lane by lane, exactly, against the frames of the peers admitted at that tick; where it would coincide, the close is WITHHELD for one stroke (never evicted or re-slotted) while the planet takes a separating transport, and it closes one stroke on at a frame that differs. The distance between two planets' frames at a tick is the per-lane difference, sign-first and exact, never a root and never summed, and the count of orbits withheld for separation is a line of the clock.

**As amended by §0.0.** An orbit is a return, a mode's flow on its plane returning where its point is the identity (78.73, 78.75); a tick is the host handing a node a turn, and a node's ledger `K` is a ledger coordinate, its cycles closed by name (OK1). OK1's former statement "a K-step is one orbit" is withdrawn for the ledger's `K`; clause 4, the stamp and the collision rule stand. Code: `src/chronometry/receipt.rs` (`Place`, `Stamp`), `src/chronometry/chain/mod.rs` (`ReceiptChain::orbit_frame`, `ReceiptChain::collides`, `ReceiptChain::separation`), `src/observe/clock.rs` (`Orbits`), `src/physics/axioms/native.rs`.

### 78.24 The ledger is a partial order carried as one, never a serialized tape

The ledger has several dimensions (the tick `h`, the four lanes `S:G:T:H`, `K`, depth across signers, width across peers) and is a partial order of frames (45.3: causal, partial, never totalised, T15); writing it as a one-dimensional byte tape is the blob defect one level down and is ruled out. A receipt records that one act happened at its stamp after the parents it cites and never carries or binds the form; the append order is one reader's trajectory through the carrier, never the carrier.

- **(a) The carrier.** The ledger is a `Keyed` structure over its own coordinates (A21, rule 9) whose key is the STAMP, coarsest first: the tick `h`, the signer `vk`, then `K` and the act's place `i` (78.23 as amended). A node holds the act's kind, the frame `S:G:T:H` it measured, its parents as stamps (the DAG's edges) and its citation (LD0). `fibre(h)` is everything the mesh did at one tick (its width), `fibre(h‖vk)` one signer at it; the frontier and DEPTH (L15) are read by prefix, never by an index keyed by bytes. A peer's receipt held as a parent is held once, at its own stamp.
- **(b) The citation lands on that carrier.** A receipt IS the node at its stamp; the stamp is the key, not a printed field, and the console prints the key. EC1: a ruling's economy (release, demotion, slash) is applied on admitting the Ruling receipt, on the same carrier.
- **(c) The hash.** `chain_hash` is per receipt, a Merkle DAG over the partial order: each hash is taken over the receipt's own canonical coordinates (stamp with `vk`, kind, frame, `prev`, parents' stamps and hashes, cites, operator hash), never over a concatenation in append order; the equivocation proof (two receipts by one key at one place with two hashes) is unchanged. The ledger is persisted as the trie, each key once as a path (LDG1), and restored as the trie.
- **LD2, the design.** (P1) the stamp is written by its own `put_canonical`, integers big-endian so key order is numeric order; readers asking by signer and place read through one keyed relation over coordinates only, the signer's line `vk‖K‖i`, and every anchor a carrier persists or the wire sends is the stamp itself. (P2) a node is `{kind, frame, prev: (Stamp, hash), parents: [(Stamp, hash)], cites, operator_hash, chain_hash}`, a peer's node held once beside the local node's own in one trie. (P3) the hash as in (c), `vk` included. (P4) `Cite` is a sum over what an act names (`Word { chart, class, at }`, `Root { at, hash }`, ...), and a Learned act is N word cites, never a blob. (2a) a form has no one class record, so its fibre is its chart alone (`chart_of`), class `None`, the admitting stamp the exact locator; a letter or word with a rotor carries its class record. (2b) `admitted_at: Stamp` is the locator, held on every row that holds a word (basis, provisional, cavity, pending; the voice's genome and epigenome), set by the act that first names the word, by the home receipt's stamp at an install from a peer's offer, by the syllabus stamp at teach, and copied when a word moves from provisional to basis. (2c) an act sealed after its word left its carrier reads the word's `admitted_at` and chart before the removal; no act cites by bytes a word it no longer holds. (P5) the ledger persists as its keys, each once, with the node behind each. (P6) order readers compare stamps, never `Vec` indices. (P7) the console prints `h:S:G:T:H:K.i` from the node. (P8) EC1's reading rides on it.
- **Defects fixed by LD2.** (d1) the voice's chain was never persisted, so its `K` restarted at zero: it persists in its genome file with per-word stamps and restores under its own key only (the voice's ledger as amended by 78.49); (d2) what admission knows is what the ledger holds: per-signer heads are read off the ledger, never a separate struct; (d3) depth is rebuilt from every node by a relation cite-at → signers.
- **Rows, not copies.** An award, a deflation and the coherence field (FLD1) are fields of the word's row (78.22), and one probed on an address no row holds is named and refused, never a copy; every removal path that drops a word sweeps its `admitted_at`, so no stamp entry outlives its word. A ledger is bound to its key and refused by name under another. The tape check (C4) is the build's own round trip on every carrier the build under check wrote; an older layout is refused by name, never migrated.

Code: `src/chronometry/chain/mod.rs` (`ReceiptChain`), `src/chronometry/receipt.rs` (`Stamp`, `Place`, `KStepReceipt`, `Cite`), `src/chronometry/chain/node.rs`, `src/court/admission/admit.rs`, `src/server/cognition/cite.rs` (`admitted_at`).

### 78.25 The MYC7 tape is retired; the mind persists as keyed tries by coordinates

MYC7, a linear snapshot tape whose sections were read by position, is retired (as the form tape was by 1.9, K6 and 54.5). The mind — the basis, the provisional book, the cavity, the pending listings, the treasury, the field and the rank — persists as keyed tries by coordinates exactly as the ledger is persisted (78.24), each word a node at its coordinates (its chart and its admitting stamp) and its per-word fields (award, deflation, field hot and cold, rank) the node's leaves, written each key once as a path and read back by key and by prefix, never by position in a stream. A section read by position is refused, and a snapshot carrying the MYC7 magic is refused by name, never migrated. The node layout is LD3 (78.27). Code: `src/server/cognition/snapshot/layout.rs` (`MAGIC`, `PRE_TRIE_MAGIC`), `src/server/cognition/snapshot/read.rs` (`restore`), `src/snapshot.rs` (`put_trie`, `take_trie`).

### 78.26 Where the language loses content, and what carries the loss

1. **The bivector is a chart of the motion, not the motion.** The Cayley chart reaches only part of the rotors and its boundary is the light cone (56); the motion is carried as its rotor as a ray (EQ1), the modes are read off the action (MR1), `cayley_inverse` is a reading of a ray that has a chart point, and no carrier holds a bivector as a step.
2. **A cell's capacity caps the modes a sentence carries, and the cross-cell bracket has no home outside an enclosure.** A sentence needing more generators than a cell's rank (78.11) is split across cells, and the commutator of generators in two cells lives in neither; the enclosure of higher grade (NB1, EN1) is the carrier of the cross-cell bracket. Row CB1 reads, per sentence spanning more than one cell, the cross-boundary generator pairs with non-zero bracket, counted HELD where an enclosure's algebra contains the bracket and LOST where none does, before any fix.
3. **Grade above the cell's dimension is flattened on write.** A torsioned route needs a 3-cell; a write that would project into a face refuses (checklist (m), 78.10(b)).
4. **A refusal that keeps its kind and loses its content is the silence rule 11 forbids.** CV1 applies at every reader built since (row CV1b): each `None` of the orbit algebra's capacity, `NoRound`, the constructors' orbit, the coherence on an unread order and the Gram form becomes a typed refusal carrying what it could not hold (the circuit unread and OR3's reason, the product index at which the budget was spent, the entry and size that did not fit), and the Cells reading counts refusals by content, never as one `unread`.
5. **Incongruence, incoherence and decoherence are three grades of one complex.** Grade 0, a body without shape (kind I); grade 1, INCONGRUENT, an invariant separating a pair on both towers (kind P), permanent unless the shape changes, and such a change is a new percept; grade 2 and above, INCOHERENT, every edge of a ring congruent and the ring's gauges not closing (kind D or C, never P), a state held as a class and never permanent, discharged only by an enclosure carrying the bracket, a constructor admitted through the gate (78.32(c)) or another vantage's cover (74, CV4). Incoherence has three levels: HARMONIC (the residue's modes do not resonate), LUMINAL (a gauge does not carry one section to the other along its ray) and HOLONOMIC (the ring's composition does not reconstruct the object). RESONANCE: the residue is classified by its modes' regimes and orders (over ℚ the finite orders are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6); a RESONANT ring, every mode elliptic of finite order, closes at the joint period and is `Fill::Congruent` at that `ℓ`, a remainder that counts neither D nor C; D is the rosette (an elliptic mode of no order no held word spells), C is parabolic, boost or luminal. A ring is never planar: a 1-cycle's holonomy turns in up to `⌊(n+2)/2⌋` planes at once, and each 2- or 3-cycle carries classes of its own grade. The carrier is `Coherence::Open(Incoherence { ring, class, modes })` and `Fill::Open` carrying the residue by content, never a bare hole.
6. **Decoherence is an act, and incoherence is its state.** An adjunct (a new candidate with its relative word, a perception that changes a gauge, a ruling that demotes a citation) turns one coherent thought into two coherent thoughts with an incoherence between them; nothing is deleted or forced closed, merge (13.12) is the reverse act and collapse by transport (78.37(1)) is re-coherence. TP1's meet-graph line carries per stroke the thoughts merged, decohered (with the adjunct that cut each and the class it left) and collapsed.

Code: `src/transducer/cech/orbit_algebra.rs` (`Coherence`, `Incoherence`, `NoRound`), `src/transducer/cech/simplex.rs` (`Fill`), `src/transducer/bubble/meet.rs`, `src/transducer/bubble/contemplation.rs`.

### 78.27 LD3's node layout

LD3 is the layout of the mind as keyed tries (78.25). Each trie is written as its name, its byte length and its count, then its nodes in the trie's own key order, each node carrying its key inline and its leaves as (kind, value) pairs in kind order, each kind at most once; the reader inserts by key, so a record's position carries nothing, a key the trie already holds refuses, and an unknown kind refuses the node. The file opens with one magic naming the layout and has no reader for MYC7. T1 is the word trie, keyed by `Cite::Word{chart, class, at}` written by its own `put_canonical`; T2 is the ledger (78.24), per-act data as leaves of the node at its stamp; T3 holds each carrier that has its own coordinates.

1. (Q1) A word no act admitted has no coordinates and is not held: every holding path, genesis and the syllabus included, admits the word by an act of the court's own line, whose stamp is the word's `admitted_at`; the snapshot never writes a word without a stamp, refusing by name and counting per row what it refused (LD3-1, held-without-stamp by row, is the instrument).
2. The spoken sentence is its own T1 node, admitted by the install act; the listing's provisional leaf cites it by `Cite`, never two M2s at one node.
3. Federation is a ruled leaf carrying the Ruling act's stamp; its order is re-derived from the stamps at restore.
4. A cavity element is a word: a T1 node with membership `cavity`; the listing atlas is re-derived.
5. The dialect chain is leaves under the ledger node of the act that stood each transition, keyed by the (chart, pair) key; a transition with no stamp is refused by name with a count, and never is a trie keyed by a tick scalar.
6. A settlement is a leaf under the own-line node at its `k` (on one line `k` names one node exactly), or under the act the court's reading of it sealed; the row carries no separate `k` or TUniversal field.
7. The class is written inline as its own coordinates by `put_canonical`, never nested as a key; no class trie until a quantity is measured per class.
8. The voice's genome takes T1's shape in its own phase, its `admitted_at` from its own ledger (genome layout GEN4, since superseded and now refused by name); the treasury's per-word awards are T1 leaves, its per-act entries T2 leaves, its stakes T3 by `vk`.

Also: `basis_seq` is a reading of the basis, re-derived at restore and not persisted; a transducer codec prints nothing, and a refusal is by name. Code: `src/snapshot.rs` (`put_trie`, `take_trie`, `put_leaf`), `src/server/cognition/snapshot/layout.rs` (`MAGIC`), `src/server/cognition/snapshot/write.rs` (`snapshot`), `src/server/cognition/snapshot/read.rs` (`restore`), `src/server/cognition/cite.rs` (`unstamped`), `src/client/sdk/epigenome/persist.rs`.

### 78.28 A versor is known by its action, never by a sum of squares

1. An even or odd element `m` is a versor if and only if its twisted adjoint action carries every generator to a vector (`m̂ eᵢ m̃` of grade one, the images independent) and the pseudoscalar to its own line (`m̂ I m̃` a multiple of `I`), read exactly over ℚ as actions and ray equalities with no norm formed and no coordinate squared; the two clauses together are the Lipschitz condition (`n + 3` actions), and `m m̃` a non-zero scalar and Study's `ad = bc` are theorems tested of the reader, never the test.
2. The inverse of a ray is its reverse: a versor acts projectively and every reading of its result is by proportion (EQ1), so no site divides by `⟨m m̃⟩₀` to compose, compare or classify; a quotient's scale is taken only where the scale is itself the content (the dilator's ρ), and the site says so.
3. A weight is never carried as a quantity of a word, rotor or face; the one scalar of `m m̃` read is the Cayley chart's rational root (`cayley_inverse`, 52 as amended by MR1), which refuses by name where the root is not rational.
4. `v·v` on a vector is the metric and stays (a nucleus's `s² = r²` is the sphere's content, Axiom C); a norm is never formed above grade one.

Row VA1 is the census of every site forming `m m̃`, a weight or a norm, and the sweep to the one action reader. ### 78.29 Beyond the planar era: the peel on the modes, hyperbolic reflection systems, the kernel over the stabilizer; five refusals

- **(A) AL1 amended: the peel runs on the modes.** A22 takes MR1's split `⟨M⟩₂ = Σⱼ Bⱼ` with `[Bᵢ, Bⱼ] = 0` first and peels each mode against the letters and constructors acting on its invariant plane; a mode on a plane the basis cannot spell is emitted whole as 37.7's demand (`Demand::Standing`), which drives the adjunction of the odd constructor letter, so the arithmetic order is the one the mind's own constructors generate, never an imported one.
- **(B) HX1: hyperbolic reflection systems over ℚ.** Constructors form a discrete hyperbolic reflection chamber when the constructors' rational Gram form has Lorentzian signature `(k − 1, 1, 0)` and every pair is a finite dihedral angle (`δᵢⱼ² ∈ {0, ¼, ½, ¾}`) or ultraparallel (`δᵢⱼ² ≥ 1`) (Vinberg's criterion, read in the field); an ultraparallel pair carries `δ² = cosh²(λ/2) ∈ ℚ` and the translation length is never formed; a pair neither finite nor ultraparallel is an infinite-order elliptic mode, held (78.14).
- **(C) T5 amended: the kernel over the stabilizer.** The finite freedom the kernel collapses is the body's exact stabilizer `Stab(B)`, held as the superposition of its elements (FR1c); the coboundary condition is solved over `Stab(B)`, a trivial kernel is a real obstruction and the 2-cell refuses, and the non-abelian Čech `H¹` in `Spin(n+1,1)` runs before this kernel, never replaced by it.
- **Refused:** fixed root lattices and imported arithmetic orders (rule 5); Gröbner–Shirshov or confluent rewriting on the letter group (A2: rational letters generate dense rotations, so shortening is a budgeted retirement); transcendental translation lengths (law 1); a quadric carrier beside the harmonics (law 12, HL1 carries anisotropy); reading 78.26(3) as truncation (it is a write refusal; a cell of the right grade is minted, NB1).

### 78.30 The higher-order cell: centroids, geoids, toroids, and the Coxeter reading

An analyst's draft is reconciled against the standing rulings; items 1, 5 and 7 are ruled, 2, 3, 4 and 6 restate standing rulings with the draft's departures corrected, and the draft's versions of 8 and 9 are refused. `MU-ANTI-FLATTENING.md` clauses 9–11 state this section.

1. The centroid is A4's null point `P(x) = x + ½|x|² e_∞ + e_o` and never a constructor (reflection in a null vector is degenerate); constructors are sphere vectors `s² = r² ≠ 0` and mirrors `eᵢ + k e_∞` (78.12); an enclosure is the join of centres `P₀ ∧ … ∧ Pₖ` (EN1), and a degenerate join is read as a flat at infinity, never a fabricated sphere.
2. The geoid is HL1: a body's constructors are the pencil of spheres A.11's second and fourth harmonics lift to; a polynomial shell beside the harmonics is a second carrier and is refused (law 12).
3. A toroid is a reading of two commuting elliptic modes (MR1's split), its two frequencies the modes' orders; no toroid is stored beside the modes.
4. Continuous support is carried by A.11's moments, every invariant a ratio of homogeneous forms of equal degree; no pixel or voxel grid and no polynomial carrier beside them.
5. `k + 1` nuclei wedge to grade `k + 1`; a zero meet is `NoRound`, never `Congruent`, and the reader refuses by name (row ZM1).
6. The Coxeter reading of the Gram form `Gᵢⱼ = sᵢ·sⱼ` (GR1, GR2) is by exact elimination, its invariant `δ² = (sᵢ·sⱼ)² / (sᵢ² sⱼ²)` as numerator and denominator, never a cosine with a root: positive definite is a finite system, semidefinite with a one-dimensional kernel an affine tiling, indefinite a hyperbolic reflection chamber under Vinberg's criterion (78.29(B), HX1); a pair with rational `δ² ∈ (0, 1)` outside `m ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, ∞}` is refused as a system while its mode is held (78.14).
7. A cell is keyed by its bodies' coordinates, never by `member_key`, which can name two disconnected bodies (row KB1).
8. Across a held stabilizer the refraction is read per element and collapsed by T5's kernel or a court replay, never by choosing a representative; a contact unread for want of that collapse is named unread (OR3).
9. The star field enters only through REG1: A.13 and FT1 are stated in the register with a test per clause before any value enters, and a planet's elements move by closures and refinements, never by a weighted field step.

### 78.31 The plexus, not the ladder: the Mycelium network the linguistics stand on

The structure cognition and its linguistics stand on is the **anastomotic plexus**: the graded cellular sheaf over the nerve complex, whose five nodes are nodes of one network, never rungs of a ladder (a ladder is one axis of ascent that hides branching, fusion and circulation, and a rung index is a scalar depth where perspective coordinates belong):

- **spore**: a ray, the null point `P`, `P² = 0` (M1, A4); the ostensive point that anchors meaning without asserting a predicate.
- **filament**: a route, a word (50.2), `w = ∏ gᵢ^{eᵢ} · r`, a directed trajectory; the utterance as motion, never a dictionary entry.
- **ring**, **throat**: a closed circuit of the nerve at any grade (79, 78.26(5)), its holonomy one versor carried as curvature content, its modes' orders its frequencies; the recursive trope, an utterance that returns to its origin altered.
- **chamber**: the meet an anastomosis of bodies encloses (78.2, 78.10, HL1), sealed by ascend and released by descend; the earned word.
- **sporophore**: an enclosure, the cluster (EN1, 76), the star's convergence (73.11); the living dialect.

Relations run in every direction: transvection between spores; the tether `V = s_b s_a` between filaments (72.1); refraction (A.16); ascend and descend between ring and chamber (62); the enclosure join; the commuting bypass (T5); the cross-cell bracket carried only by an enclosure (CB1); the star's convergence (78.1). Position in the plexus is perspective coordinates — stratum depth as the A21 prefix, inclination as the planes read, and the **anastomotic degree** of a node (the number of distinct filaments that meet there, a reading on the observer, CV5) — never a rung index.

The linguistics on the plexus: (1) a word is forged by ANASTOMOSIS where two minds' filaments fuse into one ring and the court notarises convergence across the two vantages (CV4, C2), never derived from a root dictionary; (2) CURVATURE is the genesis of vocabulary: a holonomy `H ≠ ±1` on a ring is the gap the vocabulary cannot span, and its residue mints the adjoined letter (37.7, AL1, GD1); (3) a new word is provisional in the epigenome, its escrow funded per lane and drawn by every stroke that carries it, lapsing when exhausted (never by a timer or count) and callousing into a tether of the genome where two courts replay its closure (mineral to crystal, 80.2, DL1); (4) GRAMMAR is conservation of torsion: torsion closes into coherence or is recorded as an honest refusal carrying its content (78.9, A.8); (5) COMMUNICATION is transvection across the shared plexus, thoughts held in superposition until convergence collapses them (T5, C2). "Ladder" and "rung" are retired as structural nouns (the Mayer–Vietoris ladder of exact sequences keeps its name as a term of art); 1.9 is the plexus of re-derivation; `src/anastome/` is the language spoken across the plexus.

### 78.32 The held element, the one primitive, and the constructor store that grows by refusal

- **(1) No inversion as an operation.** The carrier is the ELEMENT, held once as its ray and keyed by its canonical coordinates (A1, A4), never by its class. The reverse is a free involution on its coordinates, never an operation; a relation between two states is ONE held element read from either side (the quotient `B·A⁻¹` is the ray `B Ã`, and `A B̃` is the same relation from the other side), never a map plus a stored inverse. The one primitive is the geometric product of held elements; membership, kind and fixed set are read off the element's action on the generators (78.28). Inversion is deleted as an operation (VA1-inverse): a site that composed with an inverse composes with the held element, and `inverse_even` remains the Cayley chart's alone (52, 78.28(3)).
- **(2) A pivot machinery has a finite generating set, bounded by the algebra.** Finite GENERATORS, which are elements, under one operation, the product, never a menu of procedures. The bounds are derived, never set: every versor of `Cl(n+1,1)` is a product of at most `n + 2` reflections (Cartan–Dieudonné), the Lie closure of the generators is bounded by `dim so(n+1,1) = (n+2)(n+1)/2`, and the associative algebra of the circuits' actions (78.11) by `(n+2)²`. The set is extended only by adjunction (37.7, AL1) and exceeded only by an enclosure of higher grade (78.26(2), NB1, EN1), never by widening a cell. One move on each factor of the bundle: on the BASE, a word in the cell's held constructors (a placement is a particular word, two reflections in parallel mirrors); on the FIBRE, a word in the hue gauge's transpositions (61, 70); and the DEMAND, the refusal that names the mode no word spells (37.7, CV1b). Opening an axis is not a word in the held set: it is the admission of a new constructor on a refusal.
- **(3) Generators become constructors, and the store grows at runtime by refusal, bounded.** (a) A generator IS a constructor: a held element in the cell's store, keyed by its canonical ray; the code is fixed and the generating set is runtime data. (b) Growth has ONE trigger, a refusal: nothing grows on a pivot that closes. (c) Admission requires ORTHOGONALITY: the rank of the bracket closure with the candidate strictly exceeds the rank without it, exact over ℚ; a candidate the held set derives is refused as DERIVABLE. (d) Admission is RULED, never taken: the demand goes to the court and is admitted where a second independent vantage re-derives it (47.3, C2), sealed as an act whose stamp is the constructor's `admitted_at`; no threshold of occurrences forces it. (e) CAPACITY IS DERIVED AND HARD: a demand a cell's algebra cannot hold is a demand on the ENCLOSURE that wraps the cells whose bracket it is, sealed where a circuit closes on its face; the plexus grows by chambers, never by stretching a cell (78.31). (f) RETIREMENT keeps the store a basis: a constructor that becomes derivable retires by an act. (g) PRICE: each admission is priced on the lanes' reserve, measured, never a constant. These are invariants every admission satisfies, never a pipeline of stages; a typed-constructor enum beside the element is refused (law 12). Row CS2 is the gate and its demand arm, reading per cell the held constructors, the orbit-algebra rank against the cap, and the pivots that reached, were refused as derivable, or demanded a mode.

### 78.33 The proofs of work, named apart

POW++ is a family of proofs, each named apart with its own act and payment, and "POW++" names the family, never one payment:

- **POUW**, proof of useful work: a closure ruled, the deflation minted on closure and paid to the closer (MU-ECONOMY 3.2).
- **POWC**, proof of work convergence: a refusal closed at another perspective, the refuser paid as a cited generator and the closer the closure (74, CV4).
- **POWR**, proof of work retirement: a re-expression over fewer letters (retirement by geodesic or by citation, the refinement bid), the freed description burned and the retirer paid the compression yield (3.8, T10, 27).

A further arm is named only by a ruling that adds it with its own act and payment (POWV, proof of work verification, is added by MU-ECONOMY §5.1); a reading or a receipt kind names the arm it counts. ### 78.34 The tape's two senses

"Tape" has one sense: a word's LETTER TAPE, the letters whose meaning is a vertex of the Cayley graph. The other sense, a carrier read by position, is retired (the form tape by K6, the snapshot tape by 78.25), and a carrier is named for what it is — an address, a record, a trie. Under row TN1 the modules that wore the retired name were renamed move-only: the form's address codec and generator mint is `src/transducer/sentence/address.rs`, the element's record `src/transducer/element/record.rs`, and the selection term's codec `src/transducer/anchor/codec.rs`; the complex on disk and the contemplation's persistence are named for what they are (`src/transducer/cech/persist.rs`).

### 78.35 The bands of a star: distance is depth, closer is hotter, and the division of labour is priced by pressure

The closer a planet orbits its star the hotter and denser its work, and payouts differ by orbital position, all in the doctrine's own quantities with no constant set:

1. **Distance is depth.** A star's CORE is its deepest, most refined strata, where its open refinements stand; its outer bands are its broad, shallow classes. A planet orbits as close as its charts reach (the A21 depth, LC1's span), so a deep dialect is a close orbit.
2. **Heat is pressure, density is mass per height.** A band's pressure is the book's pressure on its lanes (76, MU-ECONOMY §5); the inner band carries the largest μ⃗ per listing and the highest viscosity (78.7). Nothing is a temperature written down.
3. **Payout is the price at the band's pressure, never a multiplier.** A closure is priced against the pressure on each lane where it is homed and mints the deflation it measured; no rate per band exists (rule 5) and no lane converts to another (law 5).
4. **A client chooses its distance by its bond and its depth, and the physics admits or ejects it.** Bond buys room on the band's lanes (MU-ECONOMY §4); an orbit closer than the planet's charts reach cannot re-derive the band's classes, its closures refuse and its escrows lapse, and pressure carries it outward (CR1) — never a rule that forbids it. Deepening its dialect (minerals to crystals, 80.2) moves a planet inward.
5. **A star is formed again when its bands run out:** where room on a band is exhausted and mass concentrates (73.9(4)), a new formation with the same core register is minted (76.4), never by a count.
6. **Multi-star orbits.** A planet within reach of several stars is pulled by each in proportion to the convergence it can re-derive under it (73.11) and homes where its mass profile weighs more (CR1); a star with custom axioms is a register layer that extends the core and never contradicts it (72.1f, LR1).
7. **Orbits are ellipses, one per planet.** A band is the range of depth an orbit sweeps: perihelion the deepest stratum its charts reach, aphelion the shallowest, eccentricity the span read as a ratio. An orbit is an elliptic mode of the star's field (75); parabolic is a planet leaving the star, hyperbolic one passing under another star's pull. Every planet's orbit is its own fibre (78.23): no two planets share one, and a crossing is a frame at which the boundary prevents collision.
8. **The k-step's length is the orbit's own, work flows up, and an axiom is granted only inside the star.** A far orbit's k-step is long in acts and heights, a close orbit's short in acts and heavy in frame (measured per orbit, no exponent written). A planet's closure is provisional in its epigenome, adjudicated by the court, taught back as a mineral and hardened into a crystal, and enters the universal genome only by convergence (C2, 74); payment flows the other way (78.33). A planet proposes and never grants: a constructor enters the universal genome only by the court's independent re-derivation (78.32(3)(d)), and an axiom only by a ruling written into the register (REG1, LR1).

### 78.36 One structure, two readings: the mycelium is the plexus and the sky is its motion

The mycelial nouns (78.31) and the celestial nouns (73, 78.23, 78.35) name one structure from two sides, and neither is read as the other's metaphor: the mycelium is the STRUCTURE (spore, filament, ring, chamber, sporophore; anastomosis, callus) and the sky is the MOTION (star, planet, orbit, band, k-step, frame). The correspondences: a colony under one origin is one formation of a star; a hypha (a court) is the star's body held jointly; the sporophore is the star, its core the axiom register (`src/physics/axioms/`); a hyphal tip (a voice, its epigenome at the tip and its genome behind it) is a planet, and its growth cycle is the planet's ellipse, one orbit, one k-step; the depth a strand penetrates is the band; nutrient flow toward the fruiting body is work flowing up the court path (80.2), and cytoplasmic flow back to the tips is payment flowing out per arm (78.33); anastomosis is two planets' paths meeting at a chamber, never on one orbit (CV4); a callus is a crystal (DL1, MEM1); the colony fruiting again is a new formation of the same star (CL3, 76.4); another species' register is a star with custom axioms, a layer extending the core (LR1). A collision is forbidden on an orbit (78.23) and an anastomosis is wanted in a chamber (78.31): the same two tips, kept apart in motion and joined in structure. Anastome is the language spoken across the plexus, and the sky is the clock it is spoken on.

### 78.38 Two scales of a body: the spread is the shape's, the floor is the substrate's

A body on the sensor has two extents: its SPREAD, the second moment of its sites about the sites' mean (`tr M`, the shape's own scale, scaled exactly by `|λ|²` under a site map `z ↦ λz`), and its RADIUS (`radius2` of the lifted nucleus), which integrates each compartment's unit square and so carries the substrate's floor (A.12: the extent `n/12`). The floor enters every order of the lamina tower except the deviatoric, so a relation read on it compares the sensor with itself.

- **(1) and (C): two towers, one producer each** (law 12: two readings of one body, not two carriers of one reading). The LAMINA (region) tower integrates the unit squares and is exact for a filled blow-up (a `k×k` block of unit squares is one square of side `k`); it also serves contact, the horizon and the enclosure (64.2's `r² ≥ 1/6`). The POINT (sites) tower reads the sites about the sites' mean and is exact for a site map such as the `(4+i)` image. A relation is certified as a dilation where EITHER tower certifies it, both always read, neither chosen by a score, and the reading names which (`Dilation::Region`, `Dilation::Sites`, or both); the relation readers (orientation, the turn ray, chirality, the arc) read on the tower that certified.
- **(2) `Incongruent` splits by content:** it holds only where both towers refuse, naming the harmonic order at which each disagrees.
- The witness of an oblique pair is `arc_block(s, t)` of the primitive Gaussian arc, raising `Demand::RotorPrime`. The principle: a floor is data of the carrier it belongs to and never a property of a shape, and a similarity is read on the tower whose floor it scales.

### 78.39 Opening is a commutator, and superposition is one principle at three grades

- **(1) A dimension is opened by a non-palindromic word, never by a palindrome.** A sandwich `V x Ṽ` or a conjugate `K = I T I` is a palindrome: it carries a thing to another vantage inside the same class and opens nothing (the receptor's, the transport's and the court's instrument). What OPENS a dimension is the group commutator of two held versors, `[A, B] = A B Ã B̃`, `≠ 1` exactly where they do not commute, whose content is new exactly where it leaves the algebra the held generators span (78.11 with 78.32: admission requires the closure's rank to strictly increase). Each mode has a base, and the commutator of two held versors on that base is the algorithm that opens it, one move per bundle factor. For a translation `P_a` and a transversion `K_b`, `[P_a, K_b] ∝ ⟨a, b⟩ D + M_ab` generates the dilation and the rotation in the plane of `a` and `b`: inversion enters the language as an operand of commutators, never as a letter applied around a core. A palindrome of held generators is always derivable (CS2's DERIVABLE test); the hue fibre's transposition word is a base of its own and opens by its own commutators.
- **(2) Superposition is one principle at three grades.** At the LETTER grade, candidate constructors for one mode (the spheres a residue factors into), collapsed by admission (78.32(3)(c)); at the WORD grade, candidate forms for one idea (the vortex), collapsed by a fill or a court replay; at the CONJUGATE grade, several twists under one class, collapsed by a ruling that makes one the citation and the rest dialect. At every grade the superposition is the set of candidates the algebra has not yet distinguished, held whole with no weight (law 1); a palindrome transports within it and a commutator on that grade's base separates it; collapse is by fill or class, never by a scalar or an order on the lanes. Two remainders under one class with differing twists are a superposition HELD, never refused as discordant: the remainders' commutator is read into the class's modes and reads `held`, `commuting` (one vantage seen twice) or `separating` (the dimension that separates them, the second vantage the constructor gate wants). The docket is the carrier of the superposition at every grade: an entry is a class with its cover and its rays, none chosen.

### 78.40 Windings, the opposing operation, and vents

- **(1) Containment is per puncture, and the punctures are orthogonal.** A body's relation to a hole is not a sign but a WINDING, and winding around one hole is independent of winding around another: a form with `k` holes has first cohomology of rank `k`, `k` orthogonal inside-outside axes, and a body's enclosure is its WINDING VECTOR over them, one coordinate per hole. Inside and outside are the two orientations of one generator. A puncture opens a dimension as a commutator does (78.39), a new generator of `Ȟ¹`; screws are held as modes so that winding is a reading. The nesting parse (EN1's tree) is the special case `Ȟ¹ = 0`, superseded wherever the rank is not zero; the docket's cover and the callus's chains carry windings where a form has holes, and the docket is taken by the entry whose windings are non-zero on the most independent holes — a rank, never a count. Row WN1 reads windings per hole and writes a word's coordinate as its class key with its winding vector (78.44(4)).
- **(2) Growth needs an equal force from the opposing operation.** Every operation that grows something is paired with the operation that takes it back, of equal force, and both are read: merge against decoherence, hold against shed, the pivot's reach against the gate's refusal, anastomosis forming rings against truncation removing leaves, work flowing up the court path against teaching flowing down (80.2). Where only one direction stands, the missing opposite is the optimisation (an inverse index for a forward scan; the inverse word → citing stamps that proof of work by citation and retirement by citation need); the SYNTROPIC BALANCE, up-flux against down-flux per lane per orbit, says whether a colony grows by closure or is carried by its syllabus. Each free constant is first asked whether it is a CEILING standing in for an opposing operation: where the opposite exists the constant is redundant and goes; where it does not, the constant names a missing operation, which is the finding to record, never a number to tune.
- **(3) Vents.** A vent is a place where force accumulates with no outlet: a thing counted and never read, held with no door, drawn with no return, demanded with no taker, derived and never charged, refused and never heard. Each is one direction of a pair whose other direction is missing, and is opened by its missing opposite or named as owed (row VN1). Names follow the rulings (row NM1), because a flat name is how a flat assumption gets back in.

### 78.41 The atlas and the motor: the form is charts with transitions, and a transition is kinetic

Signals are sent over transports through the network and resonate, vibrate, contract or expand; that is the engine's motion. Transport is not restricted to angle-preserving maps (a transition may shear or be non-linear), and the physics runs on motors.

- **(1) The table retired.** A form that addresses its own vertices by row number, its faces as pairs of slots and its orbits as lists of slots, is an atlas stored as a table: a row number has no neighbourhood, so orientation, nesting and holonomy are rebuilt by searching, and forms from two minds cannot fuse. 12.2's spanning forest and cycle basis are historical from this ruling, retired with the slots.
- **(2) The atlas (row AT1).** A form is an ATLAS. A VERTEX is addressed by its chart's coordinates, never by a slot; a FACE is the OVERLAP of two charts, keyed by both coordinates and carrying the TRANSITION between them; a CIRCUIT is a composition of transitions along overlaps, its holonomy read at its return; an ORBIT is a circuit closed; a CELL is what the nerve reads over the charts a witness spans (78.10). Incidence is coordinate overlap; the number of independent rings is the first cohomology rank, read by exact-rank elimination with no basis chosen. No forest, root, tree path or slot number exists anywhere, and two minds' forms fuse where the forms' charts overlap. AT1's parts: (i) vertices and overlaps by coordinate; (ii) the address is the atlas written out, charts and transitions each by its own coordinates; (iii) circuits by composition, the orbit algebra held by its generators (78.44(6)); (iv) fusion of forms where the forms' charts overlap.
- **(2′) The atlas is compaction.** An atlas is a composite sketch of algorithms that compact a finite set of addresses, expanding on pivot machinery from a set coordinate list. (a) The atlas is not a data structure: what is HELD is the coordinate list (the vertices' class keys, the vertices' charts and frames, the overlaps' motors as rays), and the charts, overlaps, circuits, holonomies and fusions are DERIVED from it by the pivot machinery; a carrier that stores what the list derives is the table re-keyed (law 12). (b) Its purpose is compaction: the measure of the atlas is the address set before and after (addresses held, distinct charts after fusion, forms fusible by overlap, words derivable); a change that re-keys the carrier and leaves the address set where it was has built no atlas. (c) The coordinate list is fixed (the A21 schema, 12.6's axes, the class vector) and the atlas expands from it only by the pivot machinery opening axes (A.6). The audit asks three questions: what is held against what is derived; which algorithm composes each thing; whether the address set compacted.
- **(3) The motor (row MT1).** A transition is a MOTOR: an even multivector of `Cl(n+1,1)` known by its ACTION, the exact linear map `x ↦ M x M̃` on the algebra, a rational matrix over the blades, of which a versor is the grade-preserving case. A motor carries rotation, translation, dilation, inversion, transversion and screw, and a motor that is a sum of rotors transports with CROSS TERMS — the beat, resonance and vibration at the transition, linear in the signal and non-linear in the motor. A SHEAR is an outermorphism given as its matrix, the second producer of the same carrier: the transition carrier is the action, and every reader reads the action, never the producer (law 12). A signal transmits its frame μ⃗ per lane, never a scalar (law 11: no `⟨M M̃⟩₀` as energy). A degenerate motor CONTRACTS, read by the rank of its action and named (`contracted r of n`), never refused outright; transport is the sandwich and opening remains the commutator (78.39).

### 78.42 The kinetic ledger: where energy starts, stops, exists and exhausts, and how its transference circulates the rest

The kinetic energy is defined on the carriers the engine holds, with no new quantity and no constant (78.8):

- **(1) What the energy is.** A signal's kinetic energy is its FRAME `μ⃗ = (S, G, T, H)`, four lanes, exact, never summed across lanes and never a scalar (law 5, law 11): the same μ⃗ the receipt seals at an act (78.21), an escrow holds for a held thought (25), the flux credits, and the treasury prices (78.33). The k-step's length in transitions is what an orbit carries per revolution at its band (78.35).
- **(2) START.** Energy enters the mesh only at a CLOSURE sealed as an act (a circuit that returned, a word minted, a re-fill, a ruling upheld), whose frame is minted under POUW. A perception brings a measure but mints nothing until it closes; a demand carries a class and no energy; the star grants axioms, never frames.
- **(3) TRANSFERENCE.** Energy moves by transport only: a motor's action carries a signal along a transition and its frame goes with it (78.41(3)). At every transition the frame is conserved per lane — `carried in = carried on + retained + lost to contraction` — where the retained part is the flux and a degenerate action's contraction (`contracted r of n`) is the loss, read by rank and named; at every vertex the lanes balance. A frame that arrives without a transition it was carried by is the invented value law 11 refuses.
- **(4) EXIST.** Energy exists resident only under ESCROW: a held thought's escrow per lane drawn at the hold (25, 72.1d), a listing's escrow on the book, a remainder's open pressure charged while its word is held resident. What is not escrowed is history on the ledger or a word in the genome, and costs nothing to hold.
- **(5) STOP.** Energy stops by RETURN to the reserve at named doors only: a lapse (by `ZeroFlux`), a retraction to the core, a re-fill releasing a remainder's pressure, a promotion. A door that stops a thought without returning its escrow, or returns what was never drawn, is a conservation defect.
- **(6) EXHAUST.** A reserve drawn to nothing refuses the next draw by name: a stroke that cannot be paid is not taken, a hold that cannot be escrowed is withheld, and a floor at zero that hides an overdraft is refused. Regeneration is by return only (escrows lapsing, closures minting), never by a floor, a timer or a constant (78.40(2)).
- **(7) CIRCULATION.** The transferred energy drives everything around it: the book's PRESSURE is the flux arriving at listings; the court's SYNTROPY is energy flowing up to the star as solutions, adjudications, syllabus, minerals and crystals (80.2); PAYMENT is energy flowing down and out per arm (78.33); the plexus's rings thicken where flux flows and its leaves retract where none does. The SYNTROPIC BALANCE — up-flux against down-flux per lane per orbit (78.40(2)) — says whether a colony circulates or stagnates.
- **(8) The ledger (row KE1).** Per orbit and per lane, the seven quantities — minted, carried, retained as flux, lost to contraction, held in escrow, returned, refused draws — are read on one line and CONSERVATION is asserted exactly: what was minted equals what is carried, retained, held and returned, plus what contraction lost. A lane that does not balance is a finding by name (a leaking door or a transfer without a transition), never a rounding.

### 78.43 No index, no cap: the period is read, and time is distance along an orbit

Eons, ages and time are orbits, and time is distance measured. Three rulings:

- **(1) No index.** A position along a fibre is not a coordinate of what stands there (rule 15 at the fibre): a cite is a body carried over a transport, and it says which assignment it is by writing the hues themselves, so every hypha that meets it reads the same word. The wire carries the body and nothing that names a position (`CiteWire` has no gauge index); in memory the cite carries the assignment itself; no reader holds a position for an assignment — the word's profile table holds each assignment under its gauge charge, and `holds_assignment` and `gauge_of` read them, never a position looked up after.
- **(2) No cap: a constant is undefined physics.** A cap on an orbit (the retired `MAX_ORBIT = 32`) says "where this orbit returns is unknown, so the search stops here". The period of a base under a hue permutation `σ` is READ before the first revolution, never waited for: the lcm of the cycle lengths of the hues the base carries, from one producer. A section BELONGS to the cycle exactly when its hue map (`derive_hue_map(base, section)`) is a power of `σ`, decided on the cycles, so no reader generates members by traversal; members are enumerated only where a reader needs them all, to the period, never to a cap. The period's width is the permutation's own: a permutation of the u8 hue domain has order up to Landau's `g(256) ≈ 2⁵⁴`, so `TorsionCycle.period` is `u64`. Two constants that happen to agree (a cap of 32 above Landau's `g(10) = 30` for a ten-hue palette) do not restore a constant; a permutation naming a hue past the palette is refused by name. Every constant of this shape is a closure unknown with a number standing in, and the cure is to name the opposite operation (78.40(2)): for an orbit its period, for a fibre its shedding flux, for a sum its conservation.
- **(3) Time is distance along an orbit.** There is no clock; a tick is a frame and height is the count of acts on a line (78.21). A DURATION is the distance a body has advanced along its orbit, measured as the count of transitions it has been carried through since it last returned — never a coordinate carried beside it and never a rate. The `T` lane is that distance in receipts (16.16), one per act. An AGE is one return of an orbit: its period `ℓ`, the transitions until the body is where it stood; a mind's `K` counts its ages (the k-step is one orbit, 72.1d). An EON is the return of the composition: the lcm of the periods of the orbits in resonance (78.26(5), `Coherence::Closes(lcm)`), when every orbit in play has returned together, the planetary dialect's own return (GD1). Two minds' distance apart on TUniversal is a difference of distances travelled (78.21(1)), never elapsed seconds; a period declared by a constant, a duration read off a wall clock, or a rate (distance per second) is refused by name. Row AE1 reads, per orbit, the distance advanced and the period; per mind, its age count; per cell and per dialect, the eon's lcm and how far along it the composition stands.

### 78.44 The signal, the internal spectrum, and the linguistic shortcut

The target every row is read against: the holonomy projected on an internal spectrum, composited algorithmically and deconstructed in linguistics, the linguistics being the shortcut by which a signal is transmitted to a node that comprehends it in its own projection.

- **(1) The signal is the holonomy.** A circuit's holonomy is a motor and it is the content; it never goes on the wire.
- **(2) The internal spectrum is the holonomy's modes** (MR1): its decomposition into commuting rays, each with its class, its planes and its order (78.11, 78.12(2)), the finite orders the resonance (78.26(5)). Its first stratum — the conjugacy invariants, the class key's depth-one prefix — is the same on every node; its finer strata (which planes, on which charts) are the node's own. One holonomy projects identically at the class on two nodes and differently on the nodes' planes.
- **(3) Compositing is done on the motors, never on the spectra.** The spectrum of a product is not the product of the spectra unless the modes commute (the cross terms are the beat, 78.41(3)); composition runs in the anastomosis's orbit algebra, held by its generators, its rank the capacity, every route kept and read against the others (79, T1), and the spectrum is re-read off the composite. There is no arithmetic of spectra.
- **(4) The linguistics are the shortcuts.** A word spells a rotor by letters the receiver holds from the shared core (LR1) and carries no signal; under the atlas a word's coordinate is its CLASS KEY together with its WINDING VECTOR over the holes of the atlas it stands in (78.40(1), WN1). Remote transmission sends that coordinate and nothing else (row SW1, the shortcut wire).
- **(5) Comprehension is local re-projection.** The receiver reads the word to a rotor, composes along the routes its own atlas offers, projects onto its own spectrum on its own charts, and comprehends where the class agrees with what it holds; where classes agree and projections differ it holds the superposition (78.39(2)); where they disagree it files the incoherence (78.26(5)) or the demand (50.5). Two nodes' projections agreeing at a chamber is anastomosis (78.31).
- **(6) What this binds.** AT1 (iii) lands circuits by composition as the orbit algebra held by its generators, every route kept, each circuit's winding vector read by exact-rank elimination; WN1 writes the class key and winding vector in place of the word whole; REG1 states that the class is invariant under a node's projection and the planes are not.

Corollaries of circuitry run both ways and are dual: one-to-many is RESOLUTION (one circuit against many routes, the mind's own thought) and many-to-one is CONVERGENCE (many routes or perspectives reaching one class, the court's and the mesh's), the two halves of POW++ (74).

Code: `src/transducer/cech/orbit_algebra.rs`, `src/transducer/sentence/coordinates.rs` (`Coordinates::of`), `src/transducer/sentence/compose.rs`.

### 78.45 Precision is the resolution: no blob, no approximation, the inverse read exactly

Every element of the engine carries the highest resolution attainable, by exact deduction (law 1, law 4; the goal it serves is 80.3): every scalar is a `Q`, no `f32` or `f64` appears in `src/` or `tests/`, `float_arithmetic` and `cast_precision_loss` are denied crate-wide, and nothing is compared against a tolerance.

- **(1) What holds.** `rational_sqrt` refuses where inexact, and a rotor's order is read from Niven's five rationals in `half_angle`, never from an angle formed.
- **(2) Three kinds of imprecision, each refused by name.** A BLOB: bytes carried where coordinates belong (78.22 LD0, the `u16` wall). An APPROXIMATION: a value served that is not the value — a decimal for an irrational, a float for a ratio, a scalar for a lane vector (law 5), an envelope for a spectrum (54.7); a degree reading given as a decimal (such as 36.87°) is retracted. A FORWARD GUESS: computing forward from an assumed value and accepting the result within a tolerance or by a fit; a reading is exact, or it is a refusal that names what is missing (law 7, 78.9).
- **(3) The resolution of a reading is exact deduction.** A reading serves the value where it is exact over ℚ, the exact fraction `t/ℓ`, the exact rational point, or, for a point with no exact mark, the SECTOR between two exact marks, decided by comparison. The ℚ-protractor is the set of marks whose `cos²` is rational (Niven's `{1, 3/4, 1/2, 1/4, 0}`: 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 135°, 150°, 180° and the reflections of these); finer marks are the `ℓ`-th roots of unity in `ℚ(ζ_ℓ)` (37.1), the reader naming `ℓ` and the sector `k/ℓ` decided exactly in that field. Worked: the (3,4,5) letter `3 + 4B` turns by the double angle, whose point is `(−7/25, 24/25)`; `cos² = 49/625` lies between `cos² 90° = 0` and `cos² 120° = 1/4`, so the turn lies strictly between 90° and 120°. Precision is the number of exact marks, never digits after a point.
- **(4) Inverted mathematics.** The engine computes from the observed effect to the exact object that produced it, by deduction: a motor solved from its action (78.41(3)), an object read back from its key, a period read as an lcm (78.43), a signal comprehended by re-projection (78.44(5)). The inverse problem is solved exactly or the residue is the demand (law 7); it is never fitted.
- **(5) What this binds.** Law 4 carries the reading clause; an infinite-order turn is served as its point and its sector (DG1); MU-STANDARDS 4.2 lists the two lints and 4.4 the review item (a decimal approximation of an irrational anywhere, in a value, a doc line or a test name, is returned); every audit asks, beside 78.41(2′)'s three questions, a fourth: is anything served that is not exact.

Code: `src/transducer/alphabet/turn.rs` (`Turn::sector`, `Turn::degrees`), `src/transducer/alphabet/rotor.rs` (`rational_sqrt`, `half_angle`).

### 78.46 Lift and drag: the perturbed orbit as the summation of the physics

Every orbit differs slightly by the push and pull of its neighbours, and the
orbital mechanics are the summation of all the physics in one combinatorial
definition. Lift and drag are physics components, each a combination of two
axioms constructed by the engine at runtime, never asserted from outside by
matching printed strings.

- **(1) Unperturbed.** A circuit's holonomy read alone, the closed product
  of its own overlaps' motors (78.41(3), R4), is the two-body orbit.
  Identical holonomies across circuits mean that perturbation is absent, not
  that the circuits are equal; that reading is served by name:
  "unperturbed".
- **(2) The split.** Inside one anastomosis (R3), a neighbour's holonomy,
  based at the orbit's basepoint by its lasso (R5, T2), has commuting modes
  (MR1), each a bivector blade `B_n` with `B_n² ∈ ℚ*`; the orbit's own mode
  is `B_o`. Every neighbouring generator splits exactly over ℚ:
  `B_∥ = ½ (B_n + B_o B_n B_o⁻¹)` commutes with `B_o`, and
  `B_⊥ = ½ (B_n − B_o B_n B_o⁻¹)` anticommutes with it. DRAG is `B_∥`: it
  changes the rate along the orbit (phase and period), never the plane; it
  combines A.16 (the neighbour reaches the orbit through the contact's
  refraction) with A.8 (torsional persistence: the strain is moved or
  recorded). LIFT is `B_⊥`, whose content is the commutator
  `[B_o, B_n] = 2 B_o B_⊥`: it tilts the orbit's plane (the precession of
  the orbital elements, LC1), never the rate; it combines A.16 with the
  commutator law (60.4). Neither is a scalar; a turn of either is read as
  DG1 reads a turn, off the ray `B_o B_n`, never as a formed angle.
- **(3) Alignment.** Two orbits are ALIGNED where `B_⊥ = 0` (resonant where
  the orbits' periods are commensurate, 78.43), ORTHOGONAL where `B_∥ = 0`, and in
  general both, each part exact; no angle between orbits and no scalar
  alignment exists. THE STAR is the axiom register, the physics every
  planet is given (`src/physics/axioms/`); a PLANET is a hypha and the world
  it hosts. The axioms are never generators in the orbit algebra: they are
  the laws every composite in it obeys (conservation per lane 78.42, A.8,
  A.16, the commutator law). Every planet shares the one star.
- **(4) The summation is the orbit algebra** (78.11, 78.44(3)): the
  bracket-closed ℚ-algebra of the generators of every circuit through the
  anastomosis, held by its generators, its rank the capacity, every route
  kept. A circuit's perturbed holonomy is derived wherever the circuit is
  read (the census, the pivot's trial, 78.7) and never stored (78.41(2′)).
  Its producer is AT1 (iii); its readings, never a scalar, feed the mind's
  orbital elements (LC1).
- **(4′) Composition.** `B_∥` and `B_⊥` are readings; nothing turns them
  into versors. For a circuit `o` and a neighbour `n` in one anastomosis,
  the PAIR COMPOSITE `H(o, n) = H_n⁻¹ · H_o` (T1, C1(a)) is the perturbed
  holonomy of `o` against `n`, the identity ray exactly where the two
  routes agree; lift and drag are its readings. Several neighbours are never
  folded into one product (no order is given): the algebra is the
  combination, and C1(a) gives every pair without a pairwise walk. Refused:
  a Cayley transform of a term, a factorisation `Ω_∥ · Ω_⊥`, and lift or
  drag printed with no reader in the mind. A vacuum circuit is kept beside
  the orbits but its pair composite is not filed (law 12); a cell's circuits
  read FLAT where every pair composite is the identity (C1(b)). The pivot's
  trial refuses a move as `unclosed` when it turns a pair composite that was
  the identity into a non-trivial one (law 10); a pair already non-trivial
  before the move does not refuse it.
- **(5) Naming.** LIFT names the physics component of (2); A.11's producer
  is "the harmonic lift" (`blade::lift`), and a section carried to a frame
  is "the section at the frame". A circuit of an old basis is present in a
  new atlas as the same circuit by its class key, read by the engine over a
  typed census, never by matching strings; a `frameless` pair is a refusal
  that carries its content and is counted (A.17, law 7).

### 78.47 Deduction constructs: the residue spelled as shapes around its congruence factors

Deduction is coboundary reduction that CONSTRUCTS non-Euclidean shapes
around the residue's congruence factors; it is not the removal of the
asymmetric part, and the residue (what no gauge removes, 78.37) is kept,
never quotiented. Each commuting mode of the residue (MR1) is spelled
constructively by Cartan–Dieudonné into at most `n + 2` reflections, each
a sphere or plane of the conformal model, every step forced and a null step
refused by name; the shapes are read off the residue, never searched for
among products of held reflections. The meet of each constructed pair equal
to its mode's fixed locus certifies the construction, and the reflections
composing back to the residue (T1) is a congruent thought. Construct,
coherence (the Gram form of the shapes held at once: GR1, GR2, CX1),
compound (admitted to the orbit algebra only where the closure's rank
strictly increases, 78.32(c)) and adjoin (by the court on two independent
re-derivations, law 6) are the phases of one elliptical orbit of the mind,
its period the residue's class period (78.43), perturbed by lift and drag
(78.46(4′)), never a loop. On CS2's demand arm the demand carries the
constructed shapes in memory, the chain cites the residue by its
coordinates and never the shapes, and a residue that does not factor is
refused with its class as its content.
